question: Which is not a primary flight control surface?

choices.A: Flaps.
choices.B: Stabilator.
choices.C: Ailerons.

explanation.en:
The three primary flight controls of an airplane are the ailerons, the elevator (or stabilator), and the rudder.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The stabilator, or elevator, is a primary flight control surface. Answer (C) is incorrect. Ailerons are a primary flight control surface.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 6)
explanation.kr: 1차 조종면은 도움날개, 승강타(또는 스태빌레이터), 방향타이다. 플랩은 2차 조종면에 해당한다.

question: Which device is a secondary flight control?

choices.A: Spoilers.
choices.B: Ailerons.
choices.C: Stabilators.

explanation.en:
Spoilers are high-drag devices that assist an aircraft in slowing down and losing altitude without gaining extra speed. They are common on gliders and some high-speed aircraft.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Ailerons control the roll of the aircraft and are a primary flight control surface. Answer (C) is incorrect. Stabilators function as both a horizontal stabilizer and an elevator, which makes them a primary control surface.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 6)
explanation.kr: 스포일러는 항력을 크게 만들어 속도를 줄이거나 속도 증가 없이 고도를 낮추는 2차 조종면이다. 활공기와 고속 항공기에 많이 사용된다.

question: Ground spoilers used after landing are

choices.A: more effective at low speed.
choices.B: equally effective at any speed.
choices.C: more effective at high speed.

explanation.en:
Aerodynamic drag is initially the principal source of deceleration at high speed. As the speed lowers to 60-70% of landing speed, aerodynamic drag produced by ground spoilers is of little consequence.

Answer (A) is incorrect. As the speed lowers to 60-70% of landing speed, aerodynamic drag produced by ground spoilers is of little consequence. Answer (B) is incorrect. Ground spoiler effectiveness is directly proportional to speed.

Source: (FAA-H-8080-3B Chap 15)
explanation.kr: 착륙 직후 고속에서는 공기저항이 주요 감속 수단이다. 속도가 착륙속도의 약 60~70%까지 낮아지면 지상 스포일러의 공기역학적 항력 효과는 작아진다.

question: Some aircraft are fitted with wing spoilers to decrease

choices.A: drag.
choices.B: takeoff speed.
choices.C: lift.

explanation.en:
Some aircraft require the use of spoilers. Many modern high-speed aircraft are very clean aerodynamically. Upon landing, spoilers are deployed on the top of the wing to reduce lift and improve braking performance.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Spoilers increase drag while subsequently reducing lift. Answer (B) is incorrect. Spoilers are not used on takeoff. Spoilers reduce lift, the opposite of what is required for optimal takeoff performance.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 착륙 후 날개 윗면의 스포일러를 펼치면 양력이 줄어 바퀴에 실리는 하중이 증가하고 제동 성능이 좋아진다.

question: Which of the following is not a "primary" flight control but may be used as one on high speed aircraft?

choices.A: Stabilator.
choices.B: Speed brakes.
choices.C: Spoilers.

explanation.en:
When used for roll control, the spoiler on the side of the up-going aileron extends and reduces the lift on that side, causing the wing to drop. If the spoilers are extended as speed brakes, they can still be used for roll control.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A stabilator is a primary flight control equivalent to an elevator in aircraft that do not have a fixed horizontal stabilizer. Answer (B) is incorrect. Speed brakes are exclusively a secondary flight control.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 올라가는 도움날개 쪽의 스포일러를 펼치면 그 날개의 양력이 줄어 날개가 내려간다. 속도 제동용으로 전개한 상태에서도 롤 조종에 사용할 수 있다.

question: The elevator controls movement around which axis?

choices.A: Longitudinal.
choices.B: Lateral.
choices.C: Vertical.

explanation.en:
The elevator is the primary control device for changing the pitch attitude of an airplane about the lateral axis.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Ailerons are control surfaces attached to each wing that move in the opposite direction from one another to control roll about the longitudinal axis.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The rudder controls movement of the aircraft about its vertical axis.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 6)
explanation.kr: 승강타는 가로축을 중심으로 한 피치 자세를 조종하는 1차 조종면이다.

question: In which flight condition can a T-tail aircraft be subject to a deep stall?

choices.A: Low airspeed, low angle of attack, forward CG.
choices.B: Low airspeed, high angle of attack, aft CG.
choices.C: Low airspeed, high angle of attack, forward CG.

explanation.en:
When flying at a very high angle of attack (AOA) with a low airspeed and an aft CG, a T-tail aircraft can be more susceptible to a deep stall. In this high AOA condition, the wake of the wing impinges on the tail surface and renders it almost ineffective. The wing, if fully stalled, allows its airflow to separate right after the leading edge. The wide wake of decelerated, turbulent air blankets the horizontal tail, and thus the T-tail's effectiveness is significantly diminished.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A low AOA might not blanket the tail with turbulent or "stalled air" from the wing. Answer (C) is incorrect. A forward CG might help a stalled aircraft in recovery from the stall.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 6)
explanation.kr: T자 꼬리날개 항공기는 저속·높은 받음각·후방 무게중심 조건에서 깊은 실속에 취약하다. 주날개의 박리된 후류가 수평꼬리날개를 덮으면 승강타의 기수 낮춤 효과가 크게 감소한다.

question: One of the main functions of flaps during the approach and landing is to

choices.A: decrease the angle of descent without increasing the airspeed.
choices.B: provide the same amount of lift at a slower airspeed.
choices.C: decrease lift, thus enabling a steeper-than-normal approach to be made.

explanation.en:
Extending the flaps increases the wing camber, the wing area (some types), and the angle of attack of the wing. This allows the wing to provide the same amount of lift at a slower airspeed.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Flaps increase, not decrease, the angle of descent without increasing the airspeed. Answer (C) is incorrect. Flaps increase, not decrease, lift. They also increase induced drag.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 6 & 11)
explanation.kr: 플랩을 내리면 날개의 캠버와 일부 형식의 날개 면적이 증가해 더 낮은 속도에서도 같은 양력을 얻을 수 있다.

question: Which is true regarding the use of flaps during level turns?

choices.A: The lowering of flaps increases the stall speed.
choices.B: The raising of flaps increases the stall speed.
choices.C: Raising flaps will require added forward pressure on the yoke or stick.

explanation.en:
Raising the flaps decreases the wing camber and the angle of attack of the wing. This decreases wing lift and results in a higher stall speed.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Flaps decrease, not increase, the stall speed. Answer (C) is incorrect. Raising the flaps will decrease the lift provided by the wings. Thus, back, not forward, pressure on the yoke or stick is required to maintain altitude.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 6)
explanation.kr: 플랩을 올리면 캠버와 양력이 감소하므로 실속속도가 증가한다. 수평비행을 유지하려면 필요한 받음각과 조종압력을 함께 조정해야 한다.

question: Which type of flaps are most efficient?

choices.A: Plain flaps.
choices.B: Split flaps.
choices.C: Slotted flaps.

explanation.en:
Slotted flaps increase the lift coefficient significantly more than plain or split flaps. On small aircraft, the flap hinge is located below the lower surface of the flap. When the flap is lowered, a duct forms between the flap well in the wing and the leading edge of the flap. When the slotted flap is lowered, high energy air from the lower surface is ducted to the flap's upper surface. The high energy air from the slot accelerates the upper surface boundary layer and delays airflow separation, providing a higher CL. Thus, the slotted flap produces much greater increases in maximum coefficient of lift (CL-MAX) than the plain or split flap.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Plain flaps are the least efficient type. Answer (B) is incorrect. Split flaps are less efficient than slotted flaps.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 6)
explanation.kr: 슬롯 플랩은 날개 아랫면의 고에너지 공기를 윗면으로 보내 경계층의 흐름 박리를 늦춘다. 따라서 단순 플랩이나 스플릿 플랩보다 최대양력계수를 크게 증가시킨다.

question: The angle of attack of a wing directly controls the

choices.A: angle of incidence of the wing.
choices.B: amount of airflow above and below the wing.
choices.C: distribution of pressures acting on the wing.

explanation.en:
The angle of attack of an airfoil directly controls the distribution of pressure below and above it. When a wing is at a low but positive angle of attack, most of the lift is due to the wing's negative pressure (upper surface) and downwash. NOTE: Negative pressure is any pressure less than atmospheric, and positive pressure is pressure greater than atmospheric.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The angle of incidence is a fixed relationship between the wing chord line and the longitudinal axis of the airplane and is thus unrelated to the angle of attack.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The same amount of air must flow above and below (over and under) the wing.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 받음각은 날개 위아래의 압력 분포를 직접 결정한다. 낮은 양의 받음각에서는 윗면의 낮은 압력과 공기의 아래쪽 편향이 양력 발생에 크게 기여한다.

question: A rectangular wing, as compared to other wing planforms, has a tendency to stall first at the

choices.A: wingtip, with the stall progression toward the wing root.
choices.B: wing root, with the stall progression toward the wingtip.
choices.C: center trailing edge, with the stall progression outward toward the wing root and tip.

explanation.en:
A rectangular wing, as compared to other wing planforms, has a tendency to stall first at the wing root, with the stall progression toward the wingtip. Because the wingtips and the ailerons stall later, the pilot can use aileron control in avoiding and recovering from the stall.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The wing root, not wingtip, will stall first. Answer (C) is incorrect. The wing root, not the center trailing edge, will stall first.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 직사각형 날개는 일반적으로 날개 뿌리부터 실속해 끝단으로 진행한다. 도움날개가 있는 끝단은 늦게 실속하므로 회복 중 횡조종성을 비교적 오래 유지한다.

question: An aircraft airfoil is designed to produce lift resulting from a difference in the

choices.A: negative air pressure below and a vacuum above the airfoil's surface.
choices.B: vacuum below the airfoil's surface and greater air pressure above the airfoil's surface.
choices.C: higher air pressure below the airfoil's surface and lower air pressure above the airfoil's surface.

explanation.en:
As air molecules flow over the top portion of the wing, which is cambered, they travel a greater distance than the molecules that flow over the relatively flat underside of the wing. The airflow over the top of the wing is forced to accelerate. It is this increase in velocity that causes a pressure differential, creating an area of low pressure above the wing.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Wings create areas of low pressure, not a vacuum. A vacuum by definition is an area of zero pressure. An area of negative pressure does not exist below the wing; rather, the underside of the wing is an area of high pressure. An area of low pressure, not a vacuum, exists above the top portion of the wing. Answer (B) is incorrect. Wings create areas of low pressure, not a vacuum. A vacuum by definition is an area of zero pressure. The area of greatest pressure is located on the underside of the wing with an area of low pressure forming above the wing.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 날개 위쪽 공기의 속도가 빨라지면 압력이 낮아져 아래쪽과 압력 차가 생긴다. 이 압력 차가 양력을 만드는 핵심이다.

question: Frost covering the upper surface of an airplane wing usually will cause

choices.A: the airplane to stall at an angle of attack that is higher than normal.
choices.B: the airplane to stall at an angle of attack that is lower than normal.
choices.C: drag factors so large that sufficient speed cannot be obtained for takeoff.

explanation.en:
Frost on the surface of a wing interferes with the smooth flow of air over the wing surface; i.e., parasite drag is increased. The air flowing over the wing is thus disrupted and stalls at a lower angle of attack (a higher speed) when there is frost on the wing surface.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Frost on the wing surface will usually cause the airplane to stall at a lower, not higher, angle of attack. Answer (C) is incorrect. The drag created by frost usually will not be so disruptive as to prevent the aircraft from obtaining takeoff speed.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 서리는 날개 표면의 매끄러운 흐름을 방해해 유해항력을 증가시킨다. 더 작은 받음각에서 흐름이 박리되므로 실속속도는 높아진다.

question: By changing the angle of attack of a wing, the pilot can control the airplane's

choices.A: lift, airspeed, and drag.
choices.B: lift, airspeed, and CG.
choices.C: lift and airspeed, but not drag.

explanation.en:
The pilot can control the airplane's lift, airspeed, and drag by changing the angle of attack of the wing. As the angle of attack is increased, the lift increases to the critical angle of attack, airspeed decreases, and induced drag increases with the increase in lift.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The angle of attack has no effect on the CG of an airplane. Answer (C) is incorrect. Drag, as well as lift and airspeed, is determined by the angle of attack.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 받음각을 바꾸면 양력·속도·항력을 조절할 수 있다. 임계받음각까지 받음각을 높이면 양력과 유도항력이 증가하며, 속도는 감소하는 경향이 있다.

question: When a pilot increases the angle of attack on a symmetrical airfoil, the center of pressure will

choices.A: move forward.
choices.B: move aft.
choices.C: be unchanged.

explanation.en:
An increase in the angle of attack has no effect on the center of pressure on a symmetrical wing.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The center of pressure on a symmetrical wing does not move forward with an increase in angle of attack; it is unaffected. Answer (B) is incorrect. The center of pressure on a symmetrical wing does not move aft with an increase in angle of attack; it is unaffected.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 원문은 대칭 날개에서 받음각을 증가시켜도 압력중심 위치는 변하지 않는다고 설명한다. 따라서 보기의 '변하지 않는다'가 정답이다.

question: The critical angle of attack is exceeded when

choices.A: airflow separates from the wing's trailing edge.
choices.B: a stall occurs.
choices.C: indicated airspeed equals VS0 x 1.3.

explanation.en:
Exceeding the critical angle of attack will result in a stall.

Answer (A) is incorrect. When an airfoil exceeds its critical angle of attack, the airflow separates from the airfoil, causing a stall. This separation affects the entire wing, not just the trailing edge. Answer (C) is incorrect. V50 x 1.3 is a typical approach to landing speed; it is not the result of the critical angle of attack being exceeded.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 임계받음각을 초과하면 날개 위쪽의 흐름이 박리되어 실속한다.

question: The angle of attack at which a wing stalls remains constant regardless of

choices.A: weight, dynamic pressure, bank angle, or pitch attitude.
choices.B: dynamic pressure, but varies with weight, bank angle, and pitch attitude.
choices.C: weight and pitch attitude. but varies with dynamic pressure and bank angle.

explanation.en:
The angle of attack at which a wing stalls is constant regardless of weight, bank, pitch, etc.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The stall speed, not angle of attack, varies with weight and bank angle. Answer (C) is incorrect. The stall speed, not angle of attack, varies with bank angle.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 같은 날개의 실속 받음각은 중량·경사각·피치 자세와 관계없이 일정하다. 실속속도는 달라질 수 있지만 실속을 결정하는 기준은 임계받음각이다.

question: The design maneuvering speed is

choices.A: the maximum speed an airplane can be safely stalled.
choices.B: 1.3 times the normal stalling speed.
choices.C: maximum takeoff weight divided by VS0.

explanation.en:
The maximum speed at which an airplane may be stalled safely is called the "design maneuvering speed" (VA). VA is the speed below which you can move a single flight control, one time, to its full deflection, for one axis of airplane rotation only (pitch, roll, or yaw), in smooth air, without risk of damage to the airplane.

Answer (B) is incorrect. For older general aviation aircraft (aircraft not recently designed), the design maneuvering speed is approximately 1.7, not 1.3, times the normal stalling speed.

Answer (C) is incorrect. Dividing the takeoff weight by V so does not calculate design maneuvering speed.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 설계기동속도 VA는 매끄러운 공기에서 한 축의 한 조종면을 한 번 최대 변위시켜도 구조 손상을 피하도록 정한 속도이다. 여러 축의 동시·반복 조작까지 보장하는 속도는 아니다.

question: The need to slow an aircraft below VA is brought about by the following weather phenomenon:

choices.A: High density altitude which increases the indicated stall speed.
choices.B: Turbulence which causes an increase in stall speed.
choices.C: Turbulence which causes a decrease in stall speed.

explanation.en:
Turbulence, in the form of vertical air currents, can cause severe load stress on a wing. It is wise, in extremely rough air, to reduce the speed to VA (design maneuvering speed). Speeds up to, but not exceeding, the design maneuvering speed allow an aircraft to stall prior to experiencing an increase in load factor that would exceed the limit load of the aircraft.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Changes in density altitude do not affect indicated stall speed. Answer (C) is incorrect. Turbulence increases the load factors imposed on the aircraft, which increases, not decreases, stall speed.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 난기류의 수직 기류는 받음각과 하중배수를 급격히 높일 수 있다. 기동속도 이하로 감속하면 한계하중에 도달하기 전에 실속하도록 하는 보호 효과를 기대할 수 있다.

question: Stall speed is affected by

choices.A: weight, load factor, and power.
choices.B: load factor, angle of attack, and power.
choices.C: angle of attack, weight, and air density.

explanation.en:
Stall speed may vary under different circumstances. Factors such as weight, load factor, power, center of gravity, altitude, temperature, and the presence of snow, ice, or frost on the wings affect an aircraft's stall speed.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Stall speed is not affected by the angle of attack. Answer (C) is incorrect. Stall speed is not affected by the angle of attack.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 실속속도에는 중량, 하중배수, 출력, 무게중심, 고도·온도, 날개의 눈·얼음·서리 등 여러 조건이 영향을 준다.

question: A stall will occur

choices.A: when airspeed is no longer sufficient to generate the required lift.
choices.B: when the wing reaches the critical angle of attack.
choices.C: when the critical angle of attack is exceeded.

explanation.en:
An airfoil stalls when the air can no longer flow smoothly over the top cambered surface of the wing. This phenomenon, known as early airflow separation, occurs when the wing exceeds the critical angle of attack.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A stall can occur at any airspeed, and airspeed is not a determining factor in the cause of a stall.

Answer (B) is incorrect. A wing stalls when exceeding, not reaching, the critical angle of attack.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 임계받음각을 넘으면 날개 윗면의 공기 흐름이 매끄럽게 유지되지 못하고 박리된다. 이때 실속이 발생한다.

question: An airplane will stall at the same

choices.A: angle of attack regardless of the attitude with relation to the horizon.
choices.B: airspeed regardless of the attitude with relation to the horizon.
choices.C: angle of attack and attitude with relation to the horizon.

explanation.en:
An airplane will always stall at the same angle of attack. The airplane's attitude with relation to the horizon has no significance to the stall.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The stall speed will vary with changing load factors, weight, and power. Answer (C) is incorrect. An airplane can stall in any attitude with relation to the horizon.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 실속은 특정 기수 자세가 아니라 임계받음각에서 발생한다. 수평선에 대한 자세가 달라도 같은 날개는 같은 받음각에서 실속한다.

question: In a rapid recovery from a dive, the effects of load factor would cause the stall speed to

choices.A: increase.
choices.B: decrease.
choices.C: not vary.

explanation.en:
In a rapid recovery from a dive, the load factor would be increased because of the rapid change in the angle of attack, because gravity and centrifugal force would prevent the airplane from immediately altering its flight path. Because the relative wind is opposite the flight path, the critical angle of attack will be reached at a higher airspeed.

Answer (B) is incorrect. As load factor increases, so does stall speed. Answer (C) is incorrect. As load factor increases, so does stall speed.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 급강하에서 급격히 회복하면 받음각과 하중배수가 증가한다. 비행경로가 즉시 바뀌지 못하므로 평소보다 높은 속도에서도 임계받음각에 도달해 실속할 수 있다.

question: The stalling speed of an airplane is most affected by

choices.A: changes in air density.
choices.B: variations in flight altitude.
choices.C: variations in airplane loading.

explanation.en:
Indicated stall speed is most affected by the gross weight and how it is distributed within the airplane.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Air density does not affect indicated stall speed. Answer (B) is incorrect. Flight altitude does not affect indicated stall speed.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 지시 실속속도에 가장 큰 영향을 주는 것은 항공기 총중량과 중량의 분포이다.

question: Recovery from a stall in any airplane becomes more difficult when its

choices.A: center of gravity moves aft.
choices.B: center of gravity moves forward.
choices.C: elevator trim is adjusted nose down.

explanation.en:
The recovery from a stall in any airplane becomes progressively more difficult as the airplane's center of gravity moves aft. This difficulty is due to the decreasing stability in pitch, which results in the decrease of elevator effectiveness in lowering the nose.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Recovery from a stall becomes easier, not more difficult, as the center of gravity moves forward. Answer (C) is incorrect. The center of gravity, not the elevator trim adjustment, has an effect on the stall recovery characteristics of an airplane.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 3)
explanation.kr: 무게중심이 뒤로 갈수록 피치 안정성과 기수를 낮추는 승강타 효과가 감소한다. 따라서 실속 회복이 점점 어려워진다.

question: In small airplanes, normal recovery from spins may become difficult if the

choices.A: CG is too far rearward, and rotation is around the longitudinal axis.
choices.B: CG is too far rearward, and rotation is around the CG.
choices.C: spin is entered before the stall is fully developed.

explanation.en:
Because rotation is around the CG in a spin, with a rearward CG, the control arm at the rudder is sufficiently shortened that it may make spin recovery difficult, if not impossible. Intuitively, if there is too much weight near the tail, it is also hard to get the nose down to produce an angle of attack below the critical angle.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Rotation is around the CG, not the longitudinal axis, in a spin. Answer (C) is incorrect. In order for an airplane to spin, it must first stall.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 후방 무게중심은 방향타의 유효 모멘트팔을 줄이고 기수를 내리기 어렵게 만든다. 이 때문에 스핀 회복이 어려워지거나 불가능해질 수 있다.

question: A left side slip is used to counteract a crosswind drift during the final approach for landing. An over-the-top spin would most likely occur if the controls were used in which of the following ways? Holding the stick

choices.A: in the neutral position and applying full right rudder.
choices.B: too far to the left and applying full left rudder.
choices.C: too far back and applying full right rudder.

explanation.en:
The down aileron on the inside of the turn increases drag on the wing, slowing it down and decreasing its lift, which requires more aileron application. This causes the airplane to roll. This roll may occur so quickly that it is possible for the bank to be vertical or past vertical before it can be stopped. With these control inputs, the inside wing may suddenly drop and the airplane may continue to roll to an inverted position. This is usually the beginning of a spin.

Answer (A) is incorrect. If the stick were kept in the neutral position, the airplane would descend, increasing airspeed while yawing to the right. Answer (B) is incorrect. This would lead to a slipping turn.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 8)
explanation.kr: 선회 안쪽 날개의 내려간 도움날개는 항력을 늘리고 그 날개의 속도와 양력을 줄일 수 있다. 조작이 누적되면 날개가 급격히 떨어지면서 반전 자세와 스핀으로 이어질 수 있다.

question: Which statement is true relative to changing angle of attack?

choices.A: A decrease in angle of attack will increase pressure below the wing, and decrease drag.
choices.B: An increase in angle of attack will increase drag.
choices.C: An increase in angle of attack will decrease pressure below the wing, and increase drag.

explanation.en:
As the angle of attack is increased, up to the critical angle of attack, the greater the amount of lift is developed and the greater the induced drag.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A decrease in the angle of attack will decrease, not increase, the pressure below the wing.

Answer (C) is incorrect. An increase in angle of attack will increase, not decrease, the pressure below the wing.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 임계받음각까지 받음각을 높이면 양력뿐 아니라 유도항력도 증가한다.

question: To generate the same amount of lift as altitude is increased, an airplane must be flown at

choices.A: the same true airspeed regardless of angle of attack.
choices.B: a lower true airspeed and a greater angle of attack.
choices.C: a higher true airspeed for any given angle of attack.

explanation.en:
At an altitude of 18,000 feet MSL, the air has one-half the density of air at sea level. Thus, in order to maintain the same amount of lift as altitude increases, an airplane must be flown at a higher true airspeed for any given angle of attack.

Answer (A) is incorrect. True airspeed must be increased, not remain the same, as altitude increases to generate the same amount of lift. Answer (B) is incorrect. True airspeed must be increased, not decreased, as altitude increases to generate the same amount of lift.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 고도가 높아지면 공기밀도가 감소한다. 같은 받음각에서 같은 양력을 유지하려면 진대기속도를 증가시켜야 한다.

question: A pilot who intends to maintain level flight must coordinate the angle of attack and

choices.A: thrust.
choices.B: drag.
choices.C: lift.

explanation.en:
To maintain level flight, a pilot must coordinate thrust and the angle of attack. If the angle of attack is increased, more lift will be generated so a reduction in thrust is required. If the angle of attack is reduced, lift will be reduced and more thrust will be required.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Drag is a byproduct of lift production and the basic shape of the aircraft. A change in angle of attack will change the total drag generated, but the pilot has very little control on the amount of drag produced by the aircraft in flight, especially in a clean, cruise configuration.

Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot changes the angle of attack to control the lift generated. When the total amount of lift generated is changed, a change in thrust is required to maintain straight-and-level flight.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 수평비행을 유지하려면 받음각과 추력을 함께 조절해야 한다. 받음각을 높여 저속 수평비행을 유지하는 경우와 받음각을 낮춰 고속 수평비행을 유지하는 경우를 구분한다.

question: As the angle of bank is increased, the vertical component of lift

choices.A: decreases and the horizontal component of lift increases.
choices.B: increases and the horizontal component of lift decreases.
choices.C: decreases and the horizontal component of lift remains constant.

explanation.en:
In level flight, all lift is vertical (upwards). As bank is increased, however, a portion of the airplane's lift is transferred from a vertical component to a horizontal component. Thus, the vertical component of lift decreases and the horizontal component of lift increases as the angle of bank is increased.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The vertical component of lift decreases and the horizontal component of lift increases.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The horizontal component of lift increases.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 경사각을 높이면 양력이 수직·수평 성분으로 나뉘면서 수직 성분이 감소하고 수평 성분이 증가한다.

question: Which is true regarding the forces acting on an aircraft in a steady-state descent? The sum of all

choices.A: upward forces is less than the sum of all downward forces.
choices.B: rearward forces is greater than the sum of all forward forces.
choices.C: forward forces is equal to the sum of all rearward forces.

explanation.en:
In any steady-state flight, whether level flight, climbs, or descents, the sum of all forward forces is equal to the sum of all rearward forces, and the upward forces equal the downward forces.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Upward forces are equal to, not less than, downward forces in steady-state flight. Answer (B) is incorrect. Rearward forces are equal to, not greater than, forward forces in steady-state flight.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 정상상태 비행에서는 가속도가 없으므로 힘의 합이 0이다. 정상 강하에서도 전방 힘과 후방 힘, 위쪽 힘과 아래쪽 힘이 각각 평형을 이룬다.

question: During the transition from straight-and-level flight to a climb, the angle of attack is increased and lift

choices.A: is momentarily decreased.
choices.B: remains the same.
choices.C: is momentarily increased.

explanation.en:
During the transition from straight-and-level flight to a climb, a change in lift occurs as back elevator pressure is first applied, causing an increase in the angle of attack. Lift at this moment is now greater than weight and starts the airplane's climb.

Answer (A) is incorrect. During the transition from straight-and-level flight to a climb, lift is momentarily increased, not decreased, as the angle of attack is increased. Answer (B) is incorrect. During the transition from straight-and-level flight to a climb, lift is momentarily increased, rather than remaining the same, as the angle of attack is increased.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 수평비행에서 상승으로 전환할 때 조종간을 당기면 받음각과 양력이 일시적으로 증가한다. 이 순간 양력이 중량보다 커져 상승 경로로 전환된다.

question: What changes in airplane longitudinal control must be made to maintain altitude while the airspeed is being decreased?

choices.A: Increase the angle of attack to produce more lift than drag.
choices.B: Increase the angle of attack to compensate for the decreasing lift.
choices.C: Decrease the angle of attack to compensate for the increasing drag.

explanation.en:
As airspeed decreases, the airfoils generate less lift. Accordingly, to maintain altitude, the angle of attack must be adjusted to compensate for the decrease in lift.

Answer (A) is incorrect. If the angle of attack is increased to produce more lift than weight, not drag, the airplane will begin to climb. Answer (C) is incorrect. The angle of attack must be increased, not decreased, and the objective is to compensate for the decreased lift, not increased drag.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 속도가 줄어들면 같은 받음각에서 발생하는 양력이 감소한다. 고도를 유지하려면 받음각을 높여 이를 보상해야 한다.

question: In theory, if the airspeed of an airplane is doubled while in level flight, parasite drag will become

choices.A: twice as great.
choices.B: half as great.
choices.C: four times greater.

explanation.en:
Tests show that lift and drag vary as the square of the velocity. The velocity of the air passing over the wing in flight is determined by the airspeed of the airplane. Thus, if an airplane doubles its airspeed, lift and drag will be four times greater (assuming that the angle of attack remains the same).

Answer (A) is incorrect. The relationship between parasite drag and airspeed is not linear. Answer (B) is incorrect. Parasite drag will increase, not decrease, with an increase in airspeed.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 다른 조건이 같으면 유해항력은 속도의 제곱에 비례한다. 속도가 2배가 되면 유해항력은 4배가 된다.

question: In theory, if the angle of attack and other factors remain constant and the airspeed is doubled, the lift produced at the higher speed will be

choices.A: the same as at the lower speed.
choices.B: two times greater than at the lower speed.
choices.C: four times greater than at the lower speed.

explanation.en:
If the angle of attack and other factors remain constant, lift is proportional to the square of the airplane's velocity. For example, an airplane traveling at 200 knots has four times the lift as the same airplane traveling at 100 knots.

Answer (A) is incorrect. As airspeed is doubled, lift produced is four times greater than, not the same as, at the lower speed. Answer (B) is incorrect. As airspeed is doubled, lift produced is four, not two, times greater than at the lower speed.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 받음각·밀도 등 다른 조건이 일정할 때 양력은 속도의 제곱에 비례한다. 속도를 2배로 하면 양력은 4배가 된다.

question: As airspeed decreases in level flight below that speed for maximum lift/drag ratio, total drag of an airplane

choices.A: decreases because of lower parasite drag.
choices.B: increases because of increased induced drag.
choices.C: increases because of increased parasite drag.

explanation.en:
Total drag is at a minimum for the maximum lift/drag (L/DMAX) ratio at one specific angle of attack and lift coefficient. As airspeed decreases, the induced drag will increase because a greater angle of attack is required to maintain level flight. The amount of induced drag varies inversely as the square of the airspeed.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Total drag increases, not decreases, with decreases in airspeed below L/DMAX because of increased induced drag. Answer (C) is incorrect. Parasite drag changes directly, not inversely, with airspeed. Thus, below L/Dmax. parasite drag decreases, not increases.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 최대 양항비 속도보다 느려지면 수평비행에 더 큰 받음각이 필요해 유도항력이 증가한다. 유도항력 증가가 우세해 전체 항력도 증가한다.

question: If airspeed remains constant, but the air density increases, what will be the effect on both lift and drag?

choices.A: Lift will decrease and drag will decrease.
choices.B: Drag will decrease and lift will increase.
choices.C: Lift will increase and drag will increase.

explanation.en:
Air density is a determining factor in lift production. The greater the density of the air, the greater the lift produced by an airfoil. Induced drag is a byproduct of lift production. As lift increases, induced drag increases as well.

Answer (A) is incorrect. An increase in air density results in an increase, not a decrease, in both lift and drag.

Answer (B) is incorrect. An increase in air density results in an increase in both lift and drag. An increase in lift always results in an increase of drag because induced drag increases as lift production increases.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 공기밀도가 증가하면 같은 속도에서 양력이 증가한다. 원문은 양력 발생에 수반되는 유도항력도 함께 증가한다고 설명한다.

question: What performance is characteristic of flight at maximum lift/drag ratio in a propeller-driven airplane? Maximum

choices.A: gain in altitude over a given distance.
choices.B: range and maximum distance glide.
choices.C: coefficient of lift and minimum coefficient of drag.

explanation.en:
If the airplane is operated in steady flight at L/Dmax. the total drag is at a minimum. Many important items of airplane performance are obtained in flight at L/Dmax. For a propeller-driven airplane, these items include maximum range and maximum power-off glide range.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The best angle of climb (e.g., to clear an obstacle) is at a high angle of attack with both high lift and high drag coefficients, which would not result in an L/Dmax ratio. Answer (C) is incorrect. L/Dmax is neither at the maximum coefficient of lift nor at the minimum coefficient of drag, but at a point somewhere in between.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 최대 양항비에서는 전체 항력이 최소가 된다. 프로펠러 항공기의 최대 항속거리와 무동력 최대 활공거리는 이 조건과 관련된다.

question: Both lift and drag would be increased when which of these devices are extended?

choices.A: Flaps.
choices.B: Spoilers.
choices.C: Slats.

explanation.en:
Flaps increase both lift and (induced) drag for any given angle of attack.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Spoilers decrease lift and increase drag. Answer (C) is incorrect. Slats increase the wing area, thereby increasing lift without increasing drag.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 같은 받음각에서 플랩을 펼치면 양력과 유도항력이 모두 증가한다.

question: Which is true regarding the force of lift in steady, unaccelerated flight?

choices.A: At lower airspeeds the angle of attack must be less to generate sufficient lift to maintain altitude.
choices.B: There is a corresponding indicated airspeed required for every angle of attack to generate sufficient lift to maintain altitude.
choices.C: An airfoil will always stall at the same indicated airspeed; therefore, an increase in weight will require an increase in speed to generate sufficient lift to maintain altitude.

explanation.en:
Different angles of attack provide different lift coefficients (amounts of lift). Accordingly, any given angle of attack has a corresponding airspeed to provide sufficient lift to maintain altitude.

Answer (A) is incorrect. As airspeed is reduced, the angle of attack must be increased, not decreased, to provide sufficient lift. Answer (C) is incorrect. An airfoil will always stall at the same angle of attack, not the same indicated airspeed.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 정상 비가속 비행에서 필요한 양력을 얻으려면 속도와 받음각을 서로 맞춰야 한다. 저속에서는 더 큰 받음각이 필요하다.

question: An aircraft wing is designed to produce lift resulting from a difference in the

choices.A: negative air pressure below and a vacuum above the wing's surface.
choices.B: vacuum below the wing's surface and greater air pressure above the wing's surface.
choices.C: higher air pressure below the wing's surface and lower air pressure above the wing's surface.

explanation.en:
An airplane's lift is produced by a pressure differential resulting from relatively lower (i.e., less than atmospheric) pressure above the wing and higher (i.e. , greater than atmospheric) pressure below the wing's surface.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The air pressure below the wing is relatively higher, not negative, and the pressure above the wing is lower, not a vacuum. Answer (B) is incorrect. The air pressure below the wing is relatively higher, not a vacuum, and the pressure above the wing is lower, not higher.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 날개 윗면의 상대적으로 낮은 압력과 아랫면의 높은 압력 사이의 차이가 양력을 만든다.

question: Lift on a wing is most properly defined as the

choices.A: force acting perpendicular to the relative wind.
choices.B: differential pressure acting perpendicular to the chord of the wing.
choices.C: reduced pressure resulting from a laminar flow over the upper camber of an airfoil, which acts perpendicular to the mean camber.

explanation.en:
Lift opposes the downward force of weight, is produced by the dynamic effect of the air acting on the wing, and acts perpendicular to the relative wind through the wing's center of lift.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Lift acts perpendicular to the relative wind, not the chord line. Answer (C) is incorrect. Lift is produced by pressure resulting from flow under as well as over the wing, and it acts perpendicular to relative wind, not the mean camber of the wing.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 양력은 상대풍에 수직으로 작용하는 공기력이다. 항력은 상대풍에 평행하게 작용한다.

question: To hold an airplane in level flight at airspeeds from very slow to very fast, a pilot must coordinate thrust and

choices.A: angle of incidence.
choices.B: gross weight.
choices.C: angle of attack.

explanation.en:
If a reduction in thrust and airspeed occurs, the force of gravity (weight) will overpower lift. A pilot must increase the angle of attack to generate more lift, thus compensating for the loss of thrust. If thrust and airspeed increase, lift will overpower gravity (weight), the aircraft will climb, and the pilot must decrease the angle of attack to maintain straight-and-level flight.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The angle of incidence defines the wing's chord line and its relationship to the longitudinal axis of the airplane. A pilot cannot change the angle of incidence.

Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot cannot alter the gross weight of an aircraft in flight.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 추력과 속도가 감소하면 받음각을 높여 양력 감소를 보상한다. 반대로 속도가 증가할 때는 받음각을 낮춰 수평비행을 유지한다.

question: In theory, if the airspeed of an aircraft is cut in half while in level flight, parasite drag will become

choices.A: one-third as much.
choices.B: one-half as much.
choices.C: one-fourth as much.

explanation.en:
If an aircraft in a steady flight condition at 100 knots is accelerated to 200 knots, the parasite drag becomes four times as great; therefore, if you reduce the airspeed by half, the parasite drag will be one-fourth as much.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Induced drag increases as speed goes down. Answer (B) is incorrect. Parasite drag would be one-fourth as much, not one-half as much.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 3)
explanation.kr: 유해항력은 속도의 제곱에 비례한다. 속도를 절반으로 줄이면 유해항력은 원래의 1/4이 된다.

question: On a wing, the force of lift acts perpendicular to and the force of drag acts parallel to the

choices.A: chord line.
choices.B: flightpath.
choices.C: longitudinal axis.

explanation.en:
Lift acts perpendicular to the relative wind, which is opposite the flight path. Drag acts parallel to the flight path.

Answer (A) is incorrect. There is no fixed relationship between lift and drag with respect to the chord line. Answer (C) is incorrect. There is no fixed relationship between lift and drag and the longitudinal axis.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 양력은 상대풍에 수직이며, 항력은 상대풍 및 비행경로에 평행한 방향으로 작용한다.

question: Which statement is true regarding the opposing forces acting on an airplane in steady-state level flight?

choices.A: These forces are equal.
choices.B: Thrust is greater than drag and weight and lift are equal.
choices.C: Thrust is greater than drag and lift is greater than weight.

explanation.en:
In steady-state level flight, the sum of the opposing forces is equal to zero.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Thrust is equal to, not greater than, drag in steady-state level flight. If thrust is greater than drag, airspeed will increase. Answer (C) is incorrect. Thrust is equal to, not greater than, drag and lift is equal to, not greater than, weight in steady-state level flight. If lift is greater than weight, the airplane will enter a climb.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 정상 수평비행에서는 서로 반대 방향으로 작용하는 힘들이 평형을 이루므로 합력이 0이다.

question: When transitioning from straight-and-level flight to a constant airspeed climb, the angle of attack and lift

choices.A: are increased and remain at a higher lift-to-weight ratio to maintain the climb.
choices.B: remain the same and maintain a steady state lift-to-weight ratio during the climb.
choices.C: are momentarily increased and lift returns to a steady state during the climb.

explanation.en:
During the transition from straight-and-level flight to a climb, a change in lift occurs when back elevator pressure is first applied. Raising the aircraft's nose increases the angle of attack and momentarily increases the lift. Lift at this moment is now greater than weight and starts the aircraft climbing. After the flight path is stabilized on the upward incline, the angle of attack and lift again revert to about the level flight values.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Angle of attack and lift initially increase, but after the flight path is stabilized on the upward incline, the angle of attack and lift again revert to about the level flight values. Answer (B) is incorrect. Angle of attack and lift initially increase. It is not until after the flight path is stabilized on the upward incline that the angle of attack and lift again revert to about the level flight values.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 상승 전환 초기에는 받음각과 양력이 일시적으로 증가한다. 일정 속도의 정상 상승 경로가 형성되면 받음각과 양력은 대체로 수평비행 값에 가까워진다.

question: An airplane leaving ground effect will

choices.A: experience a reduction in ground friction and require a slight power reduction.
choices.B: experience an increase in induced drag and require more thrust.
choices.C: require a lower angle of attack to maintain the same lift coefficient.

explanation.en:
An airplane leaving ground effect (a height greater than the wingspan) will 1. Require an increase in angle of attack to maintain the same lift coefficient, 2. Experience an increase in induced drag and thrust required, 3. Experience a decrease in stability and a nose-up change in moment, and 4. Produce a reduction in static source pressure and increase in indicated airspeed.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Ground friction is reduced when breaking ground, not leaving ground effect, and an increase, not decrease, in power may be required. Answer (C) is incorrect. A higher, not lower, angle of attack is required to maintain the same lift coefficient when leaving ground effect.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 지면효과에서 벗어나면 같은 양력을 위한 받음각, 유도항력, 필요추력이 증가한다. 원문은 기수 올림 모멘트와 안정성·정압원 압력 변화도 동반된다고 설명한다.

question: To produce the same lift while in ground effect as when out of ground effect, the airplane requires

choices.A: a lower angle of attack.
choices.B: the same angle of attack.
choices.C: a greater angle of attack.

explanation.en:
In ground effect, induced drag decreases due to a reduction in wingtip vortices (caused by a reduction in the wing's downwash). which alters the spanwise lift distribution and reduces the induced angle of attack. Thus, the wing will require a lower angle of attack in ground effect to produce the same lift as when out of ground effect.

Answer (B) is incorrect. A lower, not the same, angle of attack is required to maintain the same lift while in ground effect as when out of ground effect. Answer (C) is incorrect. A lower, not greater, angle of attack is required to maintain the same lift while in ground effect as when out of ground effect.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 지면효과에서는 날개끝 와류와 하강류가 줄어 유도받음각과 유도항력이 감소한다. 따라서 같은 양력을 더 작은 기하학적 받음각으로 얻을 수 있다.

question: If the same angle of attack is maintained in ground effect as when out of ground effect, lift will

choices.A: increase, and induced drag will decrease.
choices.B: decrease, and parasite drag will increase.
choices.C: increase, and induced drag will increase.

explanation.en:
In ground effect, induced drag decreases due to a reduction in wingtip vortices (caused by a reduction in the wing's downwash), which alters the spanwise lift distribution and reduces the induced angle of attack. Thus, if an airplane is brought into ground effect with a constant angle of attack, an increase in lift will result.

Answer (B) is incorrect. At the same angle of attack in ground effect as when out of ground effect, lift will increase, not decrease, and parasite drag does not significantly change in ground effect. Answer (C) is incorrect. Induced drag decreases, not increases. in ground effect.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 받음각을 일정하게 유지한 채 지면효과에 들어가면 하강류와 유도받음각이 감소한다. 그 결과 유효받음각과 양력이 증가한다.

question: Longitudinal stability involves the motion of the airplane controlled by its

choices.A: rudder.
choices.B: elevator.
choices.C: ailerons.

explanation.en:
Longitudinal stability is the quality that makes an airplane stable about its lateral (i.e., pitch) axis. This motion is controlled by the elevators.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The rudder affects the directional, not longitudinal, stability of the airplane. Answer (C) is incorrect. The ailerons affect the lateral, not longitudinal, stability of the airplane.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 세로안정성은 가로축을 중심으로 한 피치 운동에 대한 안정성이다. 이 운동은 승강타로 조종한다.

question: Longitudinal dynamic instability in an airplane can be identified by

choices.A: bank oscillations becoming progressively steeper.
choices.B: pitch oscillations becoming progressively steeper.
choices.C: trilatitudinal roll oscillations becoming progressively steeper.

explanation.en:
Dynamic stability is the overall tendency that the airplane displays after its equilibrium is disturbed. Negative dynamic stability (dynamic instability) is a property that causes oscillations set up by a statically stable airplane to become progressively greater. Longitudinal instability refers to pitch oscillations.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Roll (bank) oscillations refer to lateral, not longitudinal, stability. Answer (C) is incorrect. Roll (bank) oscillations refer to lateral, not longitudinal, stability.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 동적 불안정은 교란 후 발생한 진동의 진폭이 시간에 따라 커지는 성질이다. 세로 동적 불안정에서는 피치 진동이 점점 증가한다.

question: If the airplane attitude remains in a new position after the elevator control is pressed forward and released, the airplane displays

choices.A: neutral longitudinal static stability.
choices.B: positive longitudinal static stability.
choices.C: neutral longitudinal dynamic stability.

explanation.en:
When an airplane's attitude is momentarily displaced and it remains at its new attitude, it is said to have neutral longitudinal static stability. Longitudinal stability is the quality that makes an airplane stable about its lateral axis (pitch).

Answer (B) is incorrect. Positive longitudinal static stability is the initial tendency of the airplane to return to its original attitude after the elevator control is pressed forward and released. Answer (C) is incorrect. The longitudinal dynamic stability is the overall, not initial, tendency that the airplane displays after the elevator control is pressed forward and released. Neutral dynamic stability is indicated if the airplane attempts to return to its original state of equilibrium, but the pitch oscillations neither increase nor decrease in magnitude in time.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 교란 후 원래 자세로 돌아오거나 더 멀어지지 않고 새로운 자세에 머물면 중립 정적 안정성이다. 여기서는 피치 운동이므로 세로 중립 정적 안정성이다.

question: If the airplane attitude initially tends to return to its original position after the elevator control is pressed forward and released, the airplane displays

choices.A: positive dynamic stability.
choices.B: positive static stability.
choices.C: neutral dynamic stability.

explanation.en:
When an airplane's elevator control is pressed forward and released and its attitude initially tends to return to its original position, the airplane displays positive static stability.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Dynamic stability is the overall, not initial, tendency the airplane displays after its equilibrium is disturbed. Positive dynamic stability means the airplane will return to its original position directly, or through a series of decreasing pitch oscillations in time. Answer (C) is incorrect. Dynamic stability is the overall, not initial, tendency the airplane displays after its equilibrium is disturbed. Neutral dynamic stability means the airplane attempts to return to its original position, but the pitch oscillations neither increase nor decrease in magnitude in time.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 교란 직후 원래 자세로 돌아가려는 초기 경향은 양의 정적 안정성을 뜻한다.

question: If an airplane is loaded to the rear of its CG range, it will tend to be unstable about its

choices.A: vertical axis.
choices.B: lateral axis.
choices.C: longitudinal axis.

explanation.en:
As the CG is moved rearward, it may move behind the center of lift, in which case the airplane is said to have negative stability about its lateral axis. Recall that the CG should be forward of the center of lift and that the tail surface is designed to have negative lift.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The CG position has relatively little to do with the stability about the vertical axis. Answer (C) is incorrect. Stability about the longitudinal axis is not greatly affected by CG location. Remember that the airplane rolls about the longitudinal axis.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 무게중심이 뒤로 이동하면 세로안정성이 감소한다. 따라서 후방 무게중심 항공기는 가로축을 중심으로 한 피치 운동에서 불안정해질 수 있다.

question: If airspeed is increased during a level turn, what action would be necessary to maintain altitude? The angle of attack

choices.A: and angle of bank must be decreased.
choices.B: must be increased or angle of bank decreased.
choices.C: must be decreased or angle of bank increased.

explanation.en:
To compensate for the added lift that would result if the airspeed were increased during a turn, the angle of attack must be decreased, or the angle of bank increased, to maintain a constant altitude.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Either the angle of attack can be decreased or the angle of bank increased, not decreased, to maintain altitude as airspeed is increased in a turn. Answer (B) is incorrect. To maintain a constant altitude in a turn as the airspeed is decreased, not increased, the angle of attack must be increased or angle of bank decreased.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 수평 선회 중 속도가 증가하면 양력이 커진다. 고도를 유지하려면 받음각을 줄이거나 경사각을 증가시켜 이를 보상한다.

question: If a standard rate turn is maintained, how long would it take to turn 360°?

choices.A: 1 minute.
choices.B: 2 minutes.
choices.C: 3 minutes.

explanation.en:
A standard rate turn is one during which the heading changes at a rate of 3°/sec. Thus, a 360° turn would take 2 min. (360° + 3°/sec. = 120 sec., or 2 min.).

Answer (A) is incorrect. At standard rate, a 180°, not 360°, turn would take 1 minute. Answer (C) is incorrect. At standard rate, a 540°, not 360°, turn would take 3 minutes.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 8)
explanation.kr: 표준율 선회는 초당 3°이다. 360°를 도는 시간은 360÷3=120초, 즉 2분이다.

question: While holding the angle of bank constant in a level turn, if the rate of turn is varied the load factor would

choices.A: remain constant regardless of air density and the resultant lift vector.
choices.B: vary depending upon speed and air density provided the resultant lift vector varies proportionately.
choices.C: vary depending upon the resultant lift vector.

explanation.en:
For any given angle of bank, the rate of turn varies with the airspeed. For example, if the angle of bank is held constant and the airspeed is increased, the rate of turn will decrease and vice versa. Because of this, there is no change in centrifugal force while holding a constant angle of bank; thus, the load factor remains constant.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The rate of turn, not load factor, will vary depending on airspeed while holding a constant angle of bank. Answer (C) is incorrect. Load factor will vary depending on the resultant load, not lift, vector.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 수평 협조선회에서 경사각이 일정하면 하중배수도 일정하다. 속도를 바꾸면 선회율은 달라지지만 하중배수는 변하지 않는다.

question: Which is correct with respect to rate and radius of turn for an airplane flown in a coordinated turn at a constant altitude?

choices.A: For a specific angle of bank and airspeed, the rate and radius of turn will not vary.
choices.B: To maintain a steady rate of turn, the angle of bank must be increased as the airspeed is decreased.
choices.C: The faster the true airspeed, the faster the rate and larger the radius of turn regardless of the angle of bank.

explanation.en:
At a constant altitude in a coordinated turn, each airspeed has a specific, unvarying rate and radius of turn for each angle of bank.

Answer (B) is incorrect. You must decrease, not increase, the angle of bank when the airspeed is decreased if you are to maintain a steady rate of turn. Answer (C) is incorrect. The faster the airspeed, the slower, not faster, the rate of turn at a constant angle of bank.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 일정 고도의 협조선회에서는 속도와 경사각의 각 조합에 대응하는 선회율과 선회반경이 정해진다.

question: To increase the rate of turn and at the same time decrease the radius, a pilot should

choices.A: maintain the bank and decrease airspeed.
choices.B: increase the bank and increase airspeed.
choices.C: increase the bank and decrease airspeed.

explanation.en:
At slower airspeeds, an airplane can make a turn in less distance (smaller radius) and at a faster rate. Thus, to decrease the radius and increase the rate, a pilot should steepen the bank and decrease airspeed.

Answer (A) is incorrect. At a given angle of bank, a decrease in airspeed will increase the rate of turn and decrease the radius, but the effect will be less than that of steepening the bank and decreasing airspeed. Answer (B) is incorrect. You decrease, not increase, airspeed to decrease the turn radius.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 속도를 낮추고 경사각을 크게 하면 더 짧은 반경으로 더 빠르게 선회할 수 있다. 즉 선회율은 증가하고 선회반경은 감소한다.

question: While maintaining a constant angle of bank and altitude in a coordinated turn, an increase in airspeed will

choices.A: decrease the rate of turn resulting in a decreased load factor.
choices.B: decrease the rate of turn resulting in no change in load factor.
choices.C: increase the rate of turn resulting in no change in load factor.

explanation.en:
When in a constant bank in a coordinated turn, an increase in airspeed will decrease the rate of turn. Because the bank is held constant, there will be no change in load factor.

Answer (A) is incorrect. There is no change in load factor in a coordinated turn if the angle of bank is held constant.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The rate of turn decreases, not increases, with an increase in airspeed, and since the angle of bank is held constant, the load factor remains constant, not decreases.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 경사각과 고도를 유지한 협조선회에서 속도가 증가하면 선회율은 감소한다. 경사각이 같으므로 하중배수는 변하지 않는다.

question: Why is it necessary to increase back elevator pressure to maintain altitude during a turn? To compensate for the

choices.A: loss of the vertical component of lift.
choices.B: loss of the horizontal component of lift and the increase in centrifugal force.
choices.C: rudder deflection and slight opposite aileron throughout the turn.

explanation.en:
As you enter a turn, lift is divided into horizontal and vertical components. This division reduces the amount of vertical lift, which is opposing weight, and thus the airplane loses altitude unless additional lift is created by increasing back elevator pressure to increase the angle of attack and the vertical component of lift.

Answer (B) is incorrect. When the horizontal component of lift is less than centrifugal force, the airplane is in a skidding turn, which is corrected by increasing bank or decreasing the rate of turn (or a combination of both). Answer (C) is incorrect. Slight opposite aileron pressure may be needed in a steep bank to overcome the airplane's overbanking tendency.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 선회하면 양력의 일부가 수평 방향으로 작용해 수직 양력이 줄어든다. 고도 유지를 위해 조종간을 당겨 받음각과 전체 양력을 증가시켜야 한다.

question: To maintain altitude during a turn, the angle of attack must be increased to compensate for the decrease in the

choices.A: forces opposing the resultant component of drag.
choices.B: vertical component of lift.
choices.C: horizontal component of lift.

explanation.en:
As you enter a turn, lift is divided into horizontal and vertical components. This division reduces the amount of vertical lift, which is opposing weight, and thus the airplane loses altitude unless additional lift is created by increasing back elevator pressure to increase the angle of attack and the vertical component of lift.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The resultant component of drag is a nonsense term. Answer (C) is incorrect. As the horizontal component of lift decreases, the vertical component increases; thus, the angle of attack will need to be decreased, not increased.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 선회 중 고도를 유지하려면 감소한 수직 양력 성분을 보상해야 한다. 받음각을 증가시켜 필요한 양력을 만든다.

question: To maintain a standard rate turn as the airspeed increases, the bank angle of the aircraft will need to

choices.A: remain constant.
choices.B: increase.
choices.C: decrease.

explanation.en:
A standard rate turn, although always 3° per sec., requires higher angles of bank as airspeed increases.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A standard rate turn, although always 3° per sec., requires higher angles of bank as airspeed increases. Answer (C) is incorrect. To maintain a standard rate turn as the airspeed increases, the bank angle of the aircraft will need to increase, not decrease.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-15B)
explanation.kr: 같은 표준 선회율을 유지하려면 속도가 높을수록 더 큰 경사각이 필요하다.

question: To maintain a standard rate turn as the airspeed decreases, the bank angle of the airplane will need to

choices.A: decrease.
choices.B: increase.
choices.C: remain constant.

explanation.en:
A standard rate turn, although always 3° per sec. , requires lower angles of bank as airspeed decreases.

Answer (B) is incorrect. A standard rate turn, although always 3° per sec., requires lower angles of bank, not higher, as airspeed decreases. Answer (C) is incorrect. To maintain a standard rate turn as the airspeed decreases, the bank angle of the aircraft will need to decrease.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-15B)
explanation.kr: 속도가 낮아지면 표준 선회율을 유지하는 데 필요한 경사각도 작아진다.

question: Which factor below is the best indication of positive or negative Gs in an aircraft?

choices.A: Change in the amount of pressure by the pilot needed on the controls.
choices.B: Change in how heavy or light you feel in your seat.
choices.C: Change in control-surface effectiveness.

explanation.en:
Positive or negative load factor is most easily observed by considering how heavy or light you feel in the seat. This effect is one of the primary considerations in the design of the structure for all airplanes.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Pilot pressure on the flight controls can be affected by speed and/or load factor.

Answer (C) is incorrect. Control surface effectiveness can be affected by speed and/or load factor.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 좌석에서 몸이 무겁거나 가볍게 느껴지는 정도로 양·음의 하중배수를 가장 쉽게 감지할 수 있다.

question: If the airspeed is increased from 89 knots to 98 knots during a coordinated level 45° banked turn, the load factor will

choices.A: remain the same, but the radius of turn will increase.
choices.B: decrease, and the rate of turn will decrease.
choices.C: increase, but the rate of turn will decrease.

explanation.en:
Because the only determinant of load factor in level, coordinated turns is the amount of bank, a change in airspeed does not change the load factor. When airspeed is increased, however, the rate of turn decreases and the radius of turn increases.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The load factor will remain the same for a constant-altitude, constant-banked turn, and the rate of turn will decrease. The radius of turn, however, will increase.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The load factor will remain the same for a constant-altitude, constant-banked turn, and the rate of turn decreases. However, the radius of turn will increase.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 수평 협조선회의 하중배수는 경사각으로 결정된다. 45° 경사를 유지한 채 속도를 높이면 하중배수는 같고, 선회율은 감소하며 반경은 증가한다.

question: Which of the following would best indicate to the pilot that the load factor placed on the airframe has been increased?

choices.A: An increase in the sensation of being pushed into the seat.
choices.B: An increase in airspeed.
choices.C: More effort is required to operate the controls.

explanation.en:
Load factor can be judged by noting the seat pressure. Increases in load factor ("pulling Gs") result in increased pressure pushing you into the seat.

Answer (B) is incorrect. An increase in airspeed is not an indication of an increased load factor. In fact, airspeed often decreases with increases in load factor in balanced flight.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The feedback provided by the flight control system will vary by aircraft type and the design of the flight control system. Some flight control systems are fly-by-wire, hydraulic, or conventional cables and pulleys. Because of these factors, the pressure applied to the controls by the pilot is not an accurate method for judging load factor.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 하중배수가 증가하면 좌석에 몸이 더 강하게 눌린다. 이 좌석 압력의 증가가 하중 증가를 알려준다.

question: Limit load factor is the ratio of

choices.A: angle of attack to stall speed.
choices.B: angle of attack to power-on configuration-specific stall speed.
choices.C: maximum sustainable load to the gross weight of the airplane.

explanation.en:
Limit load factors are the highest load factors that can be expected in normal operation under various operational situations. The limit load factor is the ratio of maximum positive or negative load imposed on the aircraft to the gross weight of the aircraft.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The relationship between angle of attack and stall speed is the critical angle of attack, not the load factor. Answer (B) is incorrect. The relationship between angle of attack and stall speed is the critical angle of attack, not the load factor.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 한계하중배수는 항공기에 가해지는 최대 허용 양·음의 하중을 항공기 총중량으로 나눈 비율이다.

question: What is the limit load factor of a normal category aircraft?

explanation.en:
Aircraft designed under the category system are easily identified by a placard ih the flight deck, which states the operational category (or categories) in which the aircraft is certified. Category Normal Utility Aerobatic Limit Load Factors 3.8 to -1.52 Gs 4.4 to -1.76 Gs 6.0 to -3.0 Gs

Answer (B) is incorrect. The limit load factor of 4.4 to -1.76 Gs is for utility category aircraft. Answer (C) is incorrect. The limit load factor of 6.0 to -3.0 Gs is for aerobatic category aircraft.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 원문 분류표에서 보통급의 한계하중배수는 +3.8~-1.52 G이다. 실용급은 +4.4~-1.76 G, 곡예급은 +6~-3 G로 제시한다.

question: Which of the following best describes the category of aircraft that has a limit load factor of +4.4 to -1.76 Gs?

choices.A: Normal category.
choices.B: Utility category.
choices.C: Aerobatic category.

explanation.en:
Aircraft designed under the category system are easily identified by a placard in the flight deck, which states the operational category (or categories) in which the aircraft is certified. Category Normal Utility Aerobatic Limit Load Factors 3.8 to -1.52 Gs 4.4 to -1.76 Gs 6.0 to -3.0 Gs

Answer (A) is incorrect. The limit load factor for normal category aircraft is 3.8 to -1.52 Gs. Answer (C) is incorrect. The limit load factor for aerobatic category aircraft is 6.0 to -3.0 Gs.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 한계하중배수 +4.4~-1.76 G는 원문 분류표의 실용급(Utility category)에 해당한다.

question: Transonic airflow typically occurs in airplane speed regimes between Mach

explanation.en:
Because there is the possibility of having both subsonic and supersonic flows existing on the aircraft, it is convenient to define certain regimes of flight. Transonic airflow is defined between Mach 0.75 and 1.20.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Transonic airflow is defined between Mach 0.75 and 1.20. Answer (B) is incorrect. Transonic airflow is defined between Mach 0.75 and 1.20.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 천음속 영역에서는 항공기 주변에 아음속·초음속 흐름이 함께 존재할 수 있다. 원문은 이 영역을 마하 0.75~1.20으로 정의한다.

question: The ratio of an airplane's true airspeed to the speed of sound in the same atmospheric conditions is

choices.A: equivalent airspeed.
choices.B: transonic airflow.
choices.C: mach number.

explanation.en:
Mach number is the ratio of an airplane's true airspeed to the speed of sound in the same atmospheric conditions. The speed of sound varies with a change of altitude and temperature. At sea level with a standard temperature of 15°C, the speed of sound is 661 knots. At 40,000 with a temperature of -55°C, the speed of sound is 57 4 knots.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Equivalent airspeed is the indicated airspeed corrected for position error, installation error, and adiabatic compressibility for a particular altitude.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Airplanes operating between 0.75 and 1.20 Mach experience transonic airflow over the wings and airframe. The shock wave created by transonic airflow over the wings often alters the center of pressure, resulting in a change to the airplane's pitch attitude.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 마하수는 같은 대기 조건에서 진대기속도를 음속으로 나눈 값이다. 음속은 온도에 따라 달라지며, 원문은 표준 해면 약 661 kt와 40,000 ft 약 574 kt를 예로 든다.

question: Accelerating past critical Mach may result in the onset of compressibility effects such as

choices.A: high speed stalls.
choices.B: P factor.
choices.C: control difficulties.

explanation.en:
The critical Mach number is the highest flight speed possible without supersonic flow. As critical Mach is exceeded, an area of supersonic airflow is created and a normal shockwave forms as the boundary between the supersonic flow and the subsonic flow on the aft portion of the airfoil surface. Accelerating past critical Mach is associated with trim and stability changes and a decrease in control surface effectiveness.

Answer (A) is incorrect. High-speed stalls do not necessarily result from accelerating past critical Mach.

Answer (B) is incorrect. P-factor affects propeller-driven airplanes, which are not designed for Mach speeds.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 임계마하수를 넘으면 날개 일부에 초음속 흐름과 충격파가 생긴다. 이로 인해 트림·안정성이 바뀌고 조종면 효과가 감소할 수 있다.

question: Acceleration past critical Mach speed may cause compressibility issues such as

choices.A: asymmetric loading.
choices.B: propeller slippage.
choices.C: drag increases.

explanation.en:
The critical Mach number is the highest flight speed possible without supersonic flow. Accelerating past critical Mach is associated with a large increase in drag due to the initial formation of a weak shockwave on the wing, creating a barrier to the oncoming airflow.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Asymmetrical loading is not associated with flight near the critical Mach speed. Rather, it is most commonly referred to as P-factor (the unbalanced production of thrust created by the blades of a propeller).

Answer (B) is incorrect. Propeller slippage is not associated with flight near the critical Mach speed. Rather, it has to do with the loss in efficiency inherent in the operation of any propeller-driven aircraft, particularly with fixed-pitch propellers.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 임계마하수를 넘으면 날개에 충격파가 형성되기 시작해 압축성 항력이 크게 증가할 수 있다.

question: What could be one result of exceeding critical Mach number?

choices.A: Propeller stall.
choices.B: Reduction in drag.
choices.C: Aircraft control difficulties.

explanation.en:
The critical Mach number is the boundary between subsonic and transonic flight and is largely dependent on the wing and airfoil design. The critical Mach number is an important point in transonic flight. When shock waves form on the aircraft, airflow separation followed by buffet and aircraft control difficulties can occur.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Propeller slippage is not associated with flight near the critical Mach speed. Rather, it has to do with the loss in efficiency inherent in the operation of any propeller-driven aircraft, particularly with fixed-pitch propellers. Answer (B) is incorrect. The critical Mach number is the highest flight speed possible without supersonic flow. Accelerating past critical Mach is associated with a large increase in drag, not a reduction in drag. This is due to the initial formation of a weak shockwave on the wing, creating a barrier to the oncoming airflow.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B)
explanation.kr: 충격파가 형성되면 흐름 박리, 버핏, 조종 곤란이 생길 수 있다. 임계마하수는 날개와 에어포일 설계에 크게 좌우된다.

question: On high-speed jet transport aircraft, spoilers can be used to "spoil" lift and augment the flaps by increasing the rate of descent. What other function can spoilers be used for?

choices.A: Lowering a wing in unison with the ailerons to cause a turn in the direction of the raised spoiler.
choices.B: Lowering the wing without the ailerons to cause the wing to not twist at high speed.
choices.C: Lowering the wing to cause a turn due to the retarding effects of adverse yaw.

explanation.en:
On swept-wing high-speed jet aircraft, spoilers are often used to eliminate adverse yaw for roll control. To turn right, for example, the spoiler on the right wing is raised, destroying some of the lift and creating more drag on the right. The right wing drops, and the aircraft banks and yaws to the right.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Spoilers work in unison with the aircraft's ailerons to bank the wing and aircraft. Answer (C) is incorrect. Spoilers eliminate adverse yaw.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 6)
explanation.kr: 후퇴익 고속기는 스포일러를 롤 조종과 역요 억제에 사용할 수 있다. 오른쪽 스포일러를 올리면 오른쪽 양력이 줄고 항력이 늘어 오른쪽으로 롤·요가 발생한다.

question: Which statement is true about magnetic deviation of a compass? Deviation

choices.A: varies over time as the agonic line shifts.
choices.B: varies for different headings "of the same aircraft.
choices.C: is the same for all aircraft in the same locality.

explanation.en:
The difference between the direction indicated by a compass not installed in an airplane and one installed in an airplane is called compass deviation. Magnetic fields produced by the metal and electrical accessories in the airplane disturb the compass needle and produce errors. The amount of deviation varies with different headings.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The position of the agonic line determines magnetic variation, not compass deviation.

Answer (C) is incorrect. Compass deviation varies from aircraft to aircraft.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 8)
explanation.kr: 자차는 항공기 금속과 전기장비가 만드는 자기장 때문에 생기는 나침반 오차이다. 항공기의 기수방향에 따라 자차의 크기가 달라진다.

question: In the Northern Hemisphere, a magnetic compass will normally indicate a turn toward the north if

choices.A: a left turn is entered from a west heading.
choices.B: an aircraft is decelerated while on an east or west heading.
choices.C: an aircraft is accelerated while on an east or west heading.

explanation.en:
In the Northern Hemisphere, a magnetic compass will normally indicate a turn toward the north if an airplane is accelerated while on an east or west heading.

Answer (A) is incorrect. On turns from west headings, the compass will not reflect turning errors; i.e., it will be accurate in smooth, coordinated turns. Answer (B) is incorrect. If an airplane is decelerated while on an east or west heading, the compass would indicate a turn to the south, not north.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 8)
explanation.kr: 북반구에서 동쪽이나 서쪽으로 비행하며 가속하면 자기 나침반은 북쪽으로 선회하는 것처럼 지시한다.

question: During flight, when are the indications of a magnetic compass accurate?

choices.A: Only in straight-and-level unaccelerated flight.
choices.B: As long as the airspeed is constant.
choices.C: During turns if the bank does not exceed 18°.

explanation.en:
During flight, the magnetic compass indications can be considered accurate only when in straight-and-level, unaccelerated flight. During acceleration, deceleration, or turns, the compass card will dip and cause false readings.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Even with a constant airspeed, the magnetic compass may not be accurate during a turn.

Answer (C) is incorrect. Due to the compass card dip, the compass may not be accurate even during shallow turns.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 8)
explanation.kr: 자기 나침반은 직진 수평 비가속 비행에서 정확하게 읽을 수 있다. 가감속이나 선회 중에는 자기경사로 인한 오차가 발생한다.

question: Maximum structural cruising speed is the maximum speed at which an airplane can be operated during

choices.A: abrupt maneuvers.
choices.B: normal operations.
choices.C: flight in smooth air.

explanation.en:
The maximum structural cruising speed (VNO) is the upper limit of the green arc on the airspeed indicator. It is the maximum speed for normal operations.

Answer (A) is incorrect. VA is the design maneuvering speed, which is the rough air penetration speed and maximum speed for abrupt maneuvers. Answer (C) is incorrect. The yellow arc (VNO to VNE) is the caution range where flight is allowed only in smooth air.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 8)
explanation.kr: 최대 구조순항속도 VNO는 속도계 녹색 호의 상한이다. 정상 운용에서 허용되는 최대속도를 나타낸다.

question: Why should flight speeds above VNE be avoided?

choices.A: Excessive induced drag will result in structural failure.
choices.B: Design limit load factors may be exceeded, if gusts are encountered.
choices.C: Control effectiveness is so impaired that the aircraft becomes uncontrollable.

explanation.en:
At speeds above VNE. the design limit load factors for the airplane may be exceeded if gusts are encountered. Thus, this airspeed should never be exceeded, even in smooth air.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Induced drag decreases, not increases, as airspeed increases. Answer (C) is incorrect. Control effectiveness increases, not decreases, as airspeed increases.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 8)
explanation.kr: VNE를 넘으면 돌풍 등으로 설계 한계하중을 초과할 수 있다. 구조 손상 가능성이 있으므로 잔잔한 공기에서도 초과해서는 안 된다.

question: Which airspeed would a pilot be unable to identify by the color coding of an airspeed indicator?

choices.A: The never-exceed speed.
choices.B: The power-off stall speed.
choices.C: The maneuvering speed.

explanation.en:
The maneuvering speed (VA) is not color coded on an airspeed indicator. It is usually placarded and included in the airplane's flight manual.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The never-exceed speed is identified by the red radial line at the top of the yellow arc.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Two power-off stall speeds are represented on the airspeed indicator; the stall speeds in the landing and clean configurations are represented by the lower limits of the white and green arcs, respectively.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 8)
explanation.kr: 기동속도 VA는 보통 속도계의 색깔 표시에 포함되지 않는다. 해당 항공기의 표지판이나 비행교범에서 확인한다.

question: Calibrated airspeed is best described as indicated airspeed corrected for

choices.A: installation and instrument error.
choices.B: instrument error.
choices.C: non-standard temperature.

explanation.en:
Calibrated airspeed (CAS) is indicated airspeed corrected for installation and instrument error. An airspeed calibration chart is provided in the airplane's Pilot's Operating Handbook (POH).

Answer (B) is incorrect. Calibrated airspeed is indicated airspeed corrected for both installation and instrument error, not only for instrument error. Answer (C) is incorrect. Calibrated airspeed is indicated airspeed corrected for installation and instrument error, not for nonstandard temperature.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 8)
explanation.kr: 수정대기속도 CAS는 지시대기속도 IAS에서 계기오차와 장착·위치오차를 보정한 값이다. 보정표는 항공기 POH에 제시된다.

question: True airspeed is best described as calibrated airspeed corrected for

choices.A: installation or instrument error.
choices.B: non-standard temperature.
choices.C: altitude and nonstandard temperature.

explanation.en:
True airspeed (TAS) is calibrated airspeed corrected for pressure altitude and nonstandard temperature. Thus, TAS is calibrated airspeed corrected for density altitude.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Calibrated airspeed, not true airspeed, is indicated airspeed corrected for installation and, not or, instrument error. Answer (B) is incorrect. True airspeed is calibrated airspeed corrected for both nonstandard temperature and pressure altitude, not only nonstandard temperature.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 8)
explanation.kr: 진대기속도 TAS는 CAS에 기압고도와 비표준 온도의 영향을 보정한 값이다. 즉 공기밀도의 영향을 반영한다.

question: Structural damage or failure is more likely to occur in smooth air at speeds above

choices.A: VNO
choices.B: VA.
choices.C: VNE

explanation.en:
Never exceed speed (VNE) is a design limit speed where load factors could be exceeded with airspeeds in excess of VNE from a variety of phenomena. Operating above this speed is prohibited because it may result in damage or structural failure.

Answer (A) is incorrect. VNO is the maximum structural cruising speed. Do not exceed this speed except in smooth air.

Answer (B) is incorrect. VA is the design maneuvering speed. It is the speed below which you can move a single flight control one time to its full deflection for one axis of airplane rotation only (pitch, roll, or yaw), in smooth air, without risk of damage to the airplane.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B)
explanation.kr: VNE를 넘는 속도에서는 여러 공력 현상으로 설계 한계하중을 넘거나 구조가 파손될 수 있다. 따라서 VNE 초과 운용은 금지된다.

question: What is an advantage of an electric turn coordinator if the airplane has a vacuum system for other gyroscopic instruments?
