Answer (C) is incorrect. Runway holding position signs are placed on a runway to delineate intersecting runways, not taxiways.

Source: (AIM Para 2-3-5)
explanation.kr: 활주로 대기위치 표지는 활주로와 만나는 유도로 또는 다른 활주로와 만나는 활주로에서 대기 지점을 나타낸다.

question: The 'yellow demarcation bar' marking indicates

choices.A: runway with a displaced threshold that precedes the runway.
choices.B: a hold line from a taxiway to a runway.
choices.C: the beginning of available runway for landing on the approach side.

explanation.en:
A demarcation bar is a 3-foot-wide yellow stripe that separates a runway with a displaced threshold from a blast pad, stopway, or taxiway that precedes the runway.

Answer (B) is incorrect. A set of solid yellow and dashed yellow lines represents the hold lines between a taxiway and runway. Answer (C) is incorrect. The yellow demarcation bar delineates the beginning of the displaced threshold, which is not a landing surface.

Source: (AIM Para 2-3-4)
explanation.kr: 노란 경계선 Demarcation bar는 폭 3 ft의 노란 줄이다. 이설 시단이 있는 활주로와 그 앞의 제트분사 방호구역·정지로·유도로 등을 구분한다.

question: Which of the following best describes a destination sign?

choices.A: Indicates a runway on which the aircraft is presently located.
choices.B: Indicates the direction to the takeoff runway.
choices.C: Indicates the entrance to a taxiway from a runway.

explanation.en:
A destination sign has a yellow background with a black inscription. The destination sign indicates the direction of taxi required to reach a particular destination.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A destination sign indicates the direction of travel to a particular destination; it does not provide information on your present location. This answer choice best describes a runway position sign. Answer (C) is incorrect. Runway exit signs, not destination signs, indicate the entrance to a taxiway from a runway.

Source: (AIM Para 2-3-11)
explanation.kr: 목적지 표지는 노란 바탕에 검은 글자로 특정 목적지까지 지상활주할 방향을 알려준다.

question: 'Runway Holding Position Markings' on taxiways

choices.A: identify where aircraft are prohibited to taxi when not cleared to proceed by ground control.
choices.B: identify where aircraft are supposed to stop when not cleared to proceed onto the runway.
choices.C: allow an aircraft permission onto the runway.

explanation.en:
Runway holding position markings identify where aircraft are supposed to stop when not cleared onto the runway. When told to hold short of a runway, a pilot must come to a stop prior to the runway holding position markings and ensure no portion of his or her aircraft extends beyond them. At an uncontrolled airport, a pilot must ensure the runway is clear and confirm the area is clear of arriving or departing traffic on the runway prior to crossing the runway holding position markings.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Runway holding position markings are used at both controlled and uncontrolled airports. A clearance to cross runway holding position markings will not be available from ground control at a non-towered facility. It is, however, the PIC's responsibility to ensure the area is clear of traffic prior to crossing the runway holding position markings.

Answer (C) is incorrect. Access and/or a clearance onto an active runway can be granted only by ATC or the PIC at an uncontrolled airport after carefully ensuring the area is clear and they are safe to cross the runway holding position markings.

Source: (AIM Para 2-3-4)
explanation.kr: 활주로 진입 허가가 없으면 대기위치 표시 전에 항공기 어느 부분도 넘지 않도록 정지한다. 비관제 공항에서는 횡단 전에 활주로와 입출항 교통이 안전한지 확인한다.

question: Enhanced taxiway centerline markings are enhanced for a maximum of how many feet prior to the runway holding position markings?

explanation.en:
Enhanced taxiway centerlines will begin 150 ft. prior to the runway holding position markings to draw attention to the approaching runway entrance and holding position and to advise pilots to prepare to stop unless they have been cleared onto or across the runway by ATC.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Although the enhanced markings may be 50 ft., the maximum enhanced taxiway centerlines will begin 150 ft. from the runway holding position markings.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Although enhanced markings can often be 100 ft., the maximum enhanced taxiway centerlines will begin 150 ft. from the runway holding position markings.

Source: (AIM Para 2-3-4)
explanation.kr: 원문 기준 강화된 유도로 중심선은 활주로 대기위치 표시 150 ft 전부터 시작한다. 활주로 진입부와 정지 위치에 주의를 환기한다.

question: The purpose of an enhanced taxiway centerline is to

choices.A: identify the location of taxiing aircraft during low visibility operations.
choices.B: highlight an approaching runway holding position marking.
choices.C: supplement location signs in confirming the designation of the taxiway.

explanation.en:
The enhanced taxiway centerline warns pilots that they are approaching a runway holding position marking and should prepare to stop unless they have been cleared onto or across the runway by ATC.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Geographic position markings provide location information at points along low visibility taxi routes to help identify locations and are found left of the taxiway centerline. Answer (C) is incorrect. Surface painted location signs are used to supplement location signs to assist pilots in confirming the designation of the taxiway on which the aircraft is located.

Source: (AIM Para 2-3-4)
explanation.kr: 강화된 유도로 중심선은 활주로 대기위치에 접근 중임을 알린다. 진입·횡단 허가가 없으면 정지할 준비를 해야 한다.

question: How can you determine if another aircraft is on a collision course with your aircraft?

choices.A: The nose of each aircraft is pointed at the same point in space.
choices.B: The other aircraft will always appear to get larger and closer at a rapid rate.
choices.C: There will be no apparent relative motion between your aircraft and the other aircraft.

explanation.en:
Any aircraft that appears to have no relative motion and stays in one scan quadrant is likely to be on a collision course. Also, if a target shows no lateral or vertical movements but increases in size, take evasive action.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Even if you could determine the direction of the other airplane, you may not be able to accurately project the flight paths and speeds of the two airplanes to determine if they indeed point to the same point in space and will arrive there at the same time (i.e., collide). Answer (B) is incorrect. Aircraft on collision courses may not always appear to grow larger or to close at a rapid rate. Frequently, the degree of proximity cannot be detected.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-8)
explanation.kr: 다른 항공기의 상대 방위가 변하지 않고 같은 시야 구역에 계속 보이면 충돌 경로일 가능성이 있다. 좌우·상하 이동 없이 크기만 커지면 회피가 필요하다.

question: What is the general direction of movement of the other aircraft if during a night flight you observe a steady white light and a rotating red light ahead and at your altitude? The other aircraft is

choices.A: headed away from you.
choices.B: crossing to your left.
choices.C: approaching you head-on.

explanation.en:
A steady white light is the tail light. The other airplane is heading away from you. The rotating red light is the beacon light. The red and green wingtip position lights cannot be seen from the rear.

Answer (B) is incorrect. You would observe a steady red light if the other airplane was crossing to your left. Answer (C) is incorrect. You would see the red and green wingtip (not white) position lights if the other aircraft was approaching you head-on.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-3C Chap 10)
explanation.kr: 흰색 고정등은 꼬리등이므로 상대 항공기는 멀어지는 방향이다. 적색 회전등은 충돌방지 비콘이며, 뒤에서는 양쪽 날개끝 위치등이 보이지 않는다.

question: When in the vicinity of a VOR which is being used for navigation on VFR flights, it is important to

choices.A: make 90° left and right turns to scan for other traffic.
choices.B: exercise sustained vigilance to avoid aircraft that may be converging on the VOR from other directions.
choices.C: pass the VOR on the right side of the radial to allow room for aircraft flying in the opposite direction on the same radial.

explanation.en:
When operating VFR in highly congested areas, such as in the vicinity of a VOR that is being used for VFR navigation, you should exercise constant vigilance to avoid aircraft that may be converging on the VOR from other directions.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Ninety-degree turns (i.e., clearing turns) are appropriate prior to practicing stalls, etc. , but not while en route. Answer (C) is incorrect. There is no convention to pass on the right side of VORs or stay on the right side of airways. Federal Aviation Regulations require you to be on the centerline of the airway.

Source: (AIM Para 4-4-15)
explanation.kr: VOR 부근에는 여러 방향에서 접근하는 항공기가 모일 수 있다. VFR 비행 중에는 지속적인 외부 경계로 충돌을 예방해야 한다.

question: During a takeoff made behind a departing large jet airplane, the pilot can minimize the hazard of wingtip vortices by

choices.A: being airborne prior to reaching the jet's flightpath until able to turn clear of its wake.
choices.B: maintaining extra speed on takeoff and climbout.
choices.C: extending the takeoff roll and not rotating until well beyond the jet's rotation point.

explanation.en:
When departing behind a larger aircraft, you should rotate prior to the larger aircraft's rotation point and climb above its climb path until turning clear of its wake.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Even at maximum speed, you will probably not have enough control effectiveness to counteract the induced roll of the vortices. Answer (C) is incorrect. The vortices sink below the jet's flight path, so you want to be above them, not below them.

Source: (AIM Para 7-4-6)
explanation.kr: 큰 항공기 뒤에서 이륙할 때는 앞 항공기의 이륙 회전 지점보다 먼저 이륙하고 상승 경로 위를 유지한 뒤 후류에서 벗어난다.

question: To avoid possible wake turbulence from a large jet aircraft that has just landed prior to your takeoff, at which point on the runway should you plan to become airborne?

choices.A: Past the point where the jet touched down.
choices.B: At the point where the jet touched down, or just prior to this point.
choices.C: Approximately 500 feet prior to the point where the jet touched down.

explanation.en:
When taking off on a runway on which a large jet aircraft has just landed, plan to become airborne past the point where the jet touched down.

Answer (B) is incorrect. You should rotate past, not at or prior to, the point where the jet touched down. Answer (C) is incorrect. You should rotate past, not 500 feet prior to, where the jet touched down.

Source: (AIM Para 7-4-6)
explanation.kr: 큰 제트기가 착륙한 활주로에서 뒤이어 이륙할 때는 그 제트기의 접지 지점을 지난 뒤 공중에 뜨도록 계획한다.

question: Which procedure should you follow to avoid wake turbulence if a large jet crosses your course from left to right approximately 1 mile ahead and at your altitude?

choices.A: Make sure you are slightly above the path of the jet.
choices.B: Slow your airspeed to VA and maintain altitude and course.
choices.C: Make sure you are slightly below the path of the jet and perpendicular to the course.

explanation.en:
To avoid the wake turbulence of a large jet at your altitude, you should increase your altitude slightly to get above the flight path of the jet.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The greatest danger is induced roll, not turbulence. Answer (C) is incorrect. Flight below and behind a larger aircraft's path should be avoided.

Source: (AIM Para 7-4-6)
explanation.kr: 같은 고도에서 앞을 가로지르는 큰 제트기의 후류를 피하려면 그 비행경로보다 약간 높은 고도로 올라간다.

question: Choose the correct statement regarding wake turbulence.

choices.A: Vortex generation begins with the initiation of the takeoff roll.
choices.B: The primary hazard is loss of control because of induced roll.
choices.C: The greatest vortex strength is produced when the generating airplane is heavy, clean, and fast.

explanation.en:
The usual hazard associated with wake turbulence is the induced rolling movements, which can exceed the rolling capability of the encountering aircraft.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Vortex generation begins at the rotation point when the airplane takes off, not the initiation of the takeoff roll. Answer (C) is incorrect. The greatest vortex strength is when the generating aircraft is slow, not fast.

Source: (AIM Para 7-4-3)
explanation.kr: 후류난기류는 조우 항공기의 롤 조종 능력을 초과하는 강한 롤 운동을 일으킬 수 있다.

question: When landing behind a large aircraft, which procedure should be followed for vortex avoidance?

choices.A: Stay above its final approach flightpath all the way to touchdown.
choices.B: Stay below and to one side of its final approach flightpath.
choices.C: Stay well below its final approach flightpath and land at least 2,000 feet behind.

explanation.en:
When landing behind a large aircraft, stay above its final approach flight path all the way to touchdown; i.e., touch down beyond the touchdown point of the large aircraft.

Answer (B) is incorrect. You should stay at or above, not below, its flight path. Answer (C) is incorrect. You should stay at or above, not below, its flight path, and land beyond, not behind, its touchdown point.

Source: (AIM Para 7-4-6)
explanation.kr: 큰 항공기 뒤에 착륙할 때는 그 항공기의 최종접근 경로보다 높게 유지하고 앞 항공기의 접지 지점을 지나 착륙한다.

question: Which is true with respect to vortex circulation in the wake turbulence generated by an aircraft?

choices.A: Helicopters generate downwash turbulence only, not vortex circulation.
choices.B: The vortex strength is greatest when the generating aircraft is heavy, clean, and slow.
choices.C: When vortex circulation sinks into ground effect, it tends to dissipate rapidly and offer little danger.

explanation.en:
Airplanes produce wingtip vortices in all phases of flight. The vortex circulation and wake turbulence is at its greatest when the airplane is heavy, clean, and slow. To compensate for a heavy, clean, and slow configuration, a pilot must operate the aircraft at a higher angle of attack to produce the required lift, resulting in greater wake turbulence. This is commonplace in and around the airport environment as aircraft are operating at a high angle of attack to generate the required lift for takeoff and landing.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A helicopter in forward flight creates strong vortices that trail the helicopter in a similar fashion to the vortices generated by a large, fixed-wing airplane.

Answer (C) is incorrect. A vortex cannot sink into ground effect since ground effect is formed by the relationship of an airplane's wings to the earth's surface. It could be stated that wake turbulence generated by an airplane in ground effect is reduced.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 14)
explanation.kr: 와류는 항공기가 무겁고, 플랩 등을 접은 깨끗한 형상이며, 느리게 비행할 때 가장 강하다. 필요한 양력을 위해 큰 받음각을 사용하기 때문이다.

question: With respect to vortex circulation, which is true?

choices.A: Helicopters generate downwash turbulence, not vortex circulation.
choices.B: The vortex strength is greatest when the generating aircraft is flying fast.
choices.C: Vortex circulation generated by helicopters in forward flight trail behind in a manner similar to wingtip vortices generated by airplanes.

explanation.en:
In forward flight, helicopters produce a pair of high velocity trailing vortices similar to wing tip vortices of large fixed wing aircraft.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Helicopters create both downwash turbulence and wingtip vortices. Answer (B) is incorrect. The vortex strength is greatest when flying slow, not fast.

Source: (AIM Para 7-4-7)
explanation.kr: 헬리콥터도 전진비행 중 큰 고정익기의 날개끝 와류와 비슷한 한 쌍의 강한 후류 와류를 만든다.

question: Which is true with respect to vortex circulation?

choices.A: Helicopters generate downwash turbulence only, not vortex circulation.
choices.B: The vortex strength is greatest when the generating aircraft is heavy, clean, and slow.
choices.C: When vortex circulation sinks into ground effect, it tends to dissipate rapidly and offer little danger.

explanation.en:
The greatest vortex strength occurs when the generating aircraft is heavy, clean, and slow.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Helicopters generate both downwash turbulence and wingtip vortices. Answer (C) is incorrect. Vortices remain active in ground effect for a period of time.

Source: (AIM Para 7-4-3)
explanation.kr: 가장 강한 와류는 발생 항공기가 무겁고·깨끗한 형상이고·느릴 때 만들어진다.

question: Your flight takes you in the path of a large aircraft. In order to avoid the vortices you should fly

choices.A: at the same altitude as the large aircraft.
choices.B: below the altitude of the large aircraft.
choices.C: above the flight path of the large aircraft.

explanation.en:
When flying behind a large aircraft, stay at or above the other aircraft's flight path. Wingtip vortex turbulence tends to sink into the flight path of airplanes operating below the airplane generating the turbulence.

Answer (A) is incorrect. In order to avoid the vortices, avoid flying through another aircraft's flight path. Answer (B) is incorrect. Wingtip vortex turbulence tends to sink into the flight path of airplanes operating below the airplane generating the turbulence.

Source: (AIM Para 7-4-6, FAA-H-8083-25B)
explanation.kr: 날개끝 와류는 발생 항공기의 비행경로 아래로 가라앉는 경향이 있다. 큰 항공기 뒤에서는 그 비행경로와 같거나 더 높은 위치를 유지한다.

question: What should you expect when you are told that LAHSO operations are in effect at your destination airport?

choices.A: All aircraft must operate on an IFR clearance due to high traffic volume.
choices.B: ATC may offer a clearance to land and hold short of a specified point on the runway.
choices.C: Delays due to low IFR conditions and high traffic volume.

explanation.en:
Land and hold short operations (LAHSO) is an ATC procedure for when simultaneous operations (takeoffs and landings) are being conducted on intersecting runways. Pilots may be asked to land and hold short of an intersecting runway, an intersecting taxiway, or some other designated point on a runway.

Answer (A) is incorrect. LAHSO is an ATC procedure for when simultaneous operations (takeoffs and landings) are being conducted on intersecting runways. An IFR clearance is not required to participate in LAHSO. Answer (C) is incorrect. LAHSO clearances are only given when VFR conditions exist (there is a minimum ceiling of 1,000 ft. and 3 SM of visibility).

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 14)
explanation.kr: LAHSO는 교차하는 활주로 등에서 동시 운용을 가능하게 하는 절차이다. 착륙 후 교차 활주로·유도로 또는 지정 지점 전에 정지하도록 요구할 수 있다.

question: Who has the final authority to accept or decline any "land and hold short" (LAHSO) clearance?

choices.A: ATC tower controller.
choices.B: ATC approach controller.
choices.C: Pilot-in-command.

explanation.en:
The pilot in command has the final authority to accept or decline any LAHSO clearance. The safety and operation of the airplane remain the responsibility of the pilot. Pilots are expected to decline a LAHSO clearance if they determine it will compromise safety.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Although an ATC tower controller will issue a LAHSO clearance, the pilot in command has the final authority to accept or decline the LAHSO clearance.

Answer (B) is incorrect. ATC approach controllers do not issue landing or LAHSO clearances.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-11)
explanation.kr: LAHSO 허가의 수락·거절에 대한 최종 권한은 기장에게 있다. 안전이 저해된다고 판단하면 거절해야 한다.

question: Once a pilot-in-command accepts a "land and hold short" (LAHSO) clearance, the clearance must be adhered to, just as any other ATC clearance, unless

choices.A: an amended clearance is obtained or an emergency occurs.
choices.B: the wind changes or Available Landing Distance decreases.
choices.C: Available Landing Distance decreases or density altitude increases.

explanation.en:
If, for any reason, the pilot elects to request to land on the full length of the runway, to land on another runway, or to decline LAHSO, a pilot is expected to promptly inform air traffic, ideally even before the clearance is issued. A LAHSO clearance, once accepted, must be adhered to, just as any other ATC clearance, unless an amended clearance is obtained or an emergency occurs. A LAHSO clearance does not preclude a rejected landing.

Answer (B) is incorrect. A wind shift does not cancel a LAHSO clearance and Available Landing Distance is a fixed value that cannot spontaneously change. Answer (C) is incorrect. Available Landing Distance is a fixed value that cannot spontaneously change and a density altitude increase does not cancel a LAHSO clearance.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-11)
explanation.kr: 수락한 LAHSO 허가는 변경 허가를 받거나 비상상황이 생기지 않는 한 준수해야 한다. 다만 이 허가가 착륙 포기·복행을 금지하는 것은 아니다.

question: The commercial pilot operating as the pilot in command of an aircraft may accept or decline a land and hold short clearance (LAHSO)

choices.A: when operating for hire.
choices.B: any time.
choices.C: at night.

explanation.en:
The pilot in command has the final authority to accept or decline any LAHSO clearance. The safety and operation of the airplane remain the responsibility of the pilot, and pilots are expected to decline a LAH SO clearance if they determine it will compromise safety.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A pilot in command may accept or decline a LAHSO clearance regardless of the mission profile.

Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot in command may accept or decline a LAHSO clearance during both day and night operations.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-11)
explanation.kr: 사업용 조종사가 기장으로 운항해도 LAHSO 수락 여부를 결정할 최종 권한과 안전 책임은 기장에게 있다.

question: When should pilots decline a "land and hold short" (LAHSO) clearance?

choices.A: When it will compromise safety.
choices.B: If runway surface is contaminated.
choices.C: Only when the tower controller concurs.

explanation.en:
The pilot in command has the final authority to accept or decline a LAHSO clearance. The safety and operation of the airplane remain the responsibility of the pilot. Pilots are expected to decline a LAHSO clearance if they determine it will compromise safety.

Answer (B) is incorrect. ATC should not issue a LAHSO clearance if the runway is contaminated (e.g., snow, ice, etc.), which would affect the braking action of an airplane.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The pilot in command has the final authority to accept a LAHSO clearance whether or not the tower controller concurs.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-11)
explanation.kr: LAHSO가 안전을 해칠 수 있다고 판단하면 기장은 허가를 거절해야 한다.

question: What is the minimum visibility and ceiling required for a pilot to receive a "land and hold short" clearance?

choices.A: 3 statute miles and 1,000 feet.
choices.B: 3 nautical miles and 1,000 feet.
choices.C: 3 statute miles and 1,500 feet.

explanation.en:
You should only receive a LAHSO clearance when there is a minimum ceiling of 1,000 ft. and 3 SM visibility. The intent of having "basic" VFR weather conditions is to allow pilots to maintain visual contact with other aircraft and ground vehicle operations.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The minimum visibility and ceiling required for you to receive a LAHSO clearance is 3 SM, not 3 NM, and 1,000 ft. Answer (C) is incorrect. The minimum visibility and ceiling. required for you to receive a LAH SO clearance is 3 SM and 1,000 ft., not 1,500 ft.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-11)
explanation.kr: 원문은 LAHSO 수신 조건을 최소 운고 1,000 ft와 시정 3 SM으로 제시한다. 다른 항공기와 지상차량을 시각적으로 확인할 수 있도록 하기 위한 기준이다.

question: What information should a pilot have available when encountering LAHSO?

choices.A: FAA Advisory Circular on airport markings, signs, and LAHSO.
choices.B: Published available landing distance data for the expected destination.
choices.C: Aeronautical Information Manual content relating to LAHSO.

explanation.en:
To conduct LAHSO, pilots should become familiar with all available information concerning LAHSO at their destination airport. Pilots should have readily available the published Available Landing Distance (ALO) and runway slope information for all LAHSO runway combinations at each airport of intended landing.

Answer (A) is incorrect. There is no FAA Advisory Circular that deals with airport markings, signs, and LAHSO. Answer (C) is incorrect. Although the AIM is a useful tool for learning about LAHSO, it does not contain LAHSO information for specific airports.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-11)
explanation.kr: LAHSO 계획 시 공시된 사용가능착륙거리 ALD와 활주로 경사 정보를 즉시 확인할 수 있어야 한다.

question: To conduct LAHSO a pilot should have readily available

choices.A: runway slope information.
choices.B: published LAHSO procedure.
choices.C: current ATC guide for airport runway markings, lights, signs, LAHSO, and runway safety.

explanation.en:
To conduct LAHSO, pilots should become familiar with all available information concerning LAHSO at their destination airport. Pilots should have readily available the published Available Landing Distance (ALO) and runway slope information for all LAHSO runway combinations at each airport of intended landing.

Answer (B) is incorrect. There are no published LAHSO procedures for airports, only Available Landing Distance (ALO) information provided in the Chart Supplement. Answer (C) is incorrect. An ATC guide on airport runway markings, lights, signs, LAHSO, and runway safety will contain information about general airport operations, not operations specific to a given airport. The PIC must use information relevant to the destination airport to determine if LAHSO is in effect and if they can comply with the landing requirements.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-11)
explanation.kr: 목적지의 LAHSO 절차를 숙지하고 각 운용 조합의 ALD와 활주로 경사 자료를 준비한다.

question: Prior to accepting a "land and hold short" clearance (LAHSO) a pilot must confirm the aircraft can stop

choices.A: in the Available Landing Distance.
choices.B: prior to the intersecting taxiway.
choices.C: prior to the intersecting runway.

explanation.en:
To conduct LAHSO, pilots should become familiar with all available information concerning runway availability, length, and any specific LAHSO procedures at their destination airport. Pilots should have readily available the published Available Landing Distance (ALO) and runway slope information for all LAHSO runway combinations at each airport of intended landing.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Pilots must confirm the aircraft can come to a stop in the Available Landing Distance (ALO), not prior to an intersecting taxiway. While stopping prior to an intersecting taxiway might be part of your LAHSO clearance, the most accurate answer to this question is to ensure that you can stop within the ALO. Answer (C) is incorrect. Pilots must confirm the aircraft can come to a stop in the Available Landing Distance (ALO), not prior to an intersecting runway. While stopping prior to an intersecting runway might be part of your LAHSO clearance, the most accurate answer to this question is to ensure that you can stop within the ALO.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-11)
explanation.kr: LAHSO를 수락하기 전에 활주로 상태와 경사 등을 고려해 항공기가 공시된 ALD 안에서 정지할 수 있는지 확인해야 한다.

question:
If given a landing clearance on runway 16
and told to hold short of runway 6, how can a pilot
determine the available landing distance?

choices.A: The full runway length is available.
choices.B: Use rule of thumb to determine the distance.
choices.C: Ask the controller.

explanation.en:
To conduct land and hold short operations (LAHSO), pilots should have readily available the published Available Landing Distance (ALO) and runway slope information for all LAHSO runway combinations at each airport of intended landing. If the controller gives a LAHSO clearance and the pilot is unsure of the landing distance available, they can always ask the controller. The controller will provide the exact distance available in feet.

Answer (A) is incorrect. When a land and hold short clearance is given, the pilot is expected to hold short of a specified point on the runway. The full runway length is not available. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot should not use a rule of thumb to determine the available landing distance. The pilot should have readily available the published Available Landing Distance (ALO) for all LAHSO runway combinations at each airport of intended landing.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-11)
explanation.kr: 사용가능착륙거리는 공시된 ALD 자료로 확인한다. 거리를 확실히 모르면 관제사에게 요청할 수 있으며, 관제사는 사용가능 거리를 피트로 알려준다.

question: A 'land and hold short' (LAHSO) clearance

choices.A: precludes a "Go Around" by ATC.
choices.B: does not preclude a rejected landing.
choices.C: requires a runway exit at the first taxiway.

explanation.en:
Once a LAHSO is accepted, it must be adhered to unless an amended clearance is obtained or when an emergency occurs. A LAHSO does not preclude a rejected landing.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A LAHSO clearance does not preclude a rejected landing. Answer (C) is incorrect. A LAHSO requires the aircraft to stop at the hold line or exit at any taxiway instructed to by ATC. This taxiway exit would be before the LAHSO hold line.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-11)
explanation.kr: LAHSO는 수락 후 변경 허가나 비상이 없으면 준수해야 한다. 필요 시 착륙을 포기하거나 복행하는 것까지 금지하지는 않는다.

question: You are on approach to land on Runway 19 of a non-towered airport. You observe ripples on the southeast side of a small lake 3/4 mi. east of the airport. What is the most appropriate course of action?

choices.A: Proceed with your approach to Runway 19.
choices.B: Maneuver for an approach to Runway 01.
choices.C: Check the wind sock to determine the appropriate runway.

explanation.en:
Checking the wind sock would enable you to verify the wind direction over the field and determine the best runway for landing.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Landing on Runway 19 would put you in a tailwind condition. Answer (B) is incorrect. Although landing on Runway 01 would allow you to land in a headwind, it is advisable to check the wind sock to ensure that the winds on the field agree with the wind direction over the lake.

Source: (AIM Para 4-3-4)
explanation.kr: 호수의 물결 같은 간접 단서만으로 활주로를 결정하지 말고 풍향계를 확인한다. 공항의 실제 바람을 확인해야 적절한 착륙 활주로를 선택할 수 있다.

question: When making routine transponder code changes, pilots should avoid inadvertent selection of which codes?

explanation.en:
Some special codes set aside for emergencies should be avoided during routine VFR flights. They are 7500 for hijacking, 7600 for lost radio communications, and 7700 for a general emergency. Additionally, you should know that code 7777 is reserved for military interceptors.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Code 7200 may be assigned by ATC. Answer (B) is incorrect. Code 7000 may be assigned by ATC.

Source: (AIM Para 4-1-20)
explanation.kr: 일반 코드 변경 중에는 7500 납치·7600 통신두절·7700 비상 코드가 우발적으로 선택되지 않게 한다. 7777은 군용 요격기용으로 예약된다.

question: When making routine transponder code changes, pilots should avoid inadvertent selection of which code?

explanation.en:
Some special codes set aside for emergencies should be avoided during routine VFR flights. They are 7500 for hijacking, 7600 for lost radio communications, and 7700 for a general emergency. Additionally, you should know that code 7777 is reserved for military interceptors.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Code 1200 is the standard VFR code. Answer (C) is incorrect. The number 4096 is the number of possible codes, not an actual code itself. Additionally, the transponder digits only go up to 7, so a 9 is not possible.

Source: (AIM Para 4-1-20)
explanation.kr: 일상적인 트랜스폰더 조작 중에는 비상·특수 코드의 우발적 선택을 피한다. 7500은 납치, 7600은 통신두절, 7700은 일반 비상이다.

question: At an altitude below 18,000 feet MSL, which transponder code should be selected?

choices.A: Mode A/3, Code 1200.
choices.B: Mode F, Code 1200.
choices.C: Mode C, Code 4096.

explanation.en:
The standard VFR transponder code is 1200. Because all flight operations above 18,000 feet MSL are to be IFR, code 1200 is not used above that height.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The standard VFR transponder code is 1200, but Mode F is not a valid transponder type.

Answer (C) is incorrect. Mode C is a valid transponder type, but 4096 is the number of possible codes, not an actual code itself. Additionally, the transponder digits only go up to 7, so a 9 is not possible.

Source: (AIM Para 4-1-20)
explanation.kr: 미국의 표준 VFR 트랜스폰더 코드는 1200이다. 원문은 18,000 ft MSL 이상이 IFR 공역이므로 그 위에서는 VFR 코드 1200을 사용하지 않는다고 설명한다.

question: Unless otherwise authorized, if flying a transponder equipped aircraft, a pilot should squawk which VFR code?

explanation.en:
A pilot flying a transponder-equipped aircraft should set that transponder on code (squawk) 1200, which is the VFR code.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Code 7600 is the lost communication code. Answer (C) is incorrect. Code 7700 is the general emergency code.

Source: (AIM Para 4-1-20)
explanation.kr: 별도 지시가 없을 때 미국 VFR 항공기의 기본 트랜스폰더 코드는 1200이다.

question: What is the appropriate transponder code in response to lost communications?

explanation.en:
Code 7600 is used in the event of a radio failure or lost communications. Other emergency codes are 7500 for hijacking and 7700 for a general emergency. Additionally, code 7777 is reserved for military interceptors.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Code 7 400 is reserved for an unmanned aircraft experiencing a lost link. Answer (B) is incorrect. Code 7500 is used in the event of unlawful interference or hijacking.

Source: (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 4-1-20)
explanation.kr: 무선 고장이나 통신두절 시에는 7600을 설정한다. 7500은 납치, 7700은 일반 비상과 구분한다.

question: In the event of unlawful interference or hijacking, which transponder code should you input immediately?

explanation.en:
The nondiscrete transponder code 7500 is used in the event of unlawful interference or hijacking. Once input, this code triggers a special emergency indicator in all radar ATC facilities.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Code 7600 is used in the event of a radio failure or lost communications. Answer (C) is incorrect. Code 7777 is the highest value code that may be entered on a 4096 transponder and a discrete code reserved for military interceptor operations.

Source: (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 4-1-20)
explanation.kr: 불법방해·납치 상황에서는 7500을 설정한다. 이 코드는 레이더 관제시설에 특수 비상 표시를 발생시킨다.

question: A pilot mistakenly entered transponder code 7500 in response to an emergency. The correct code would have been

explanation.en:
Nondiscrete code 7700 is used to communicate an emergency, whereas 7500 should only be used in response to unlawful interference or hijacking.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Code 7777 is reserved for military interceptor operations, 7500 is for unlawful interference or hijacking, and the correct code for an emergency is 7700.

Answer (C) is incorrect. Code 7600 is reserved for radio failure or lost communications, 7500 is used for unlawful interference or hijacking, and the correct code for an emergency is 7700.

Source: (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 4-1-20)
explanation.kr: 일반 비상상황에는 7700을 사용한다. 7500은 불법방해·납치 상황을 위한 코드이다.

question: What is the hijack code?

explanation.en:
Transponder code 7500 means: "I am being hijacked/forced to a new destination." Code 7500 will never be assigned by ATC without prior notification from the pilot that his or her airplane is being subjected to unlawful interference. Code 7500 will trigger special emergency indicators in all radar ATC facilities.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Code 7200 is used for normal operating procedures. Answer (C) is incorrect. Under no circumstances should a pilot of a civil airplane operate the transponder on Code 7777. This code is reserved for military interceptor operations.

Source: (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 4-1-20)
explanation.kr: 납치 상황을 나타내는 코드는 7500이다. 관제시설에는 특수 비상 경고가 표시된다.

question: The performance tables of an aircraft for takeoff and climb are based on

choices.A: pressure/density altitude.
choices.B: cabin altitude.
choices.C: true altitude.

explanation.en:
Performance tables of an aircraft for takeoff, climb, cruise, and landing are based on pressure and/or density altitude. They are an index to the efficiency of airplane performance at various air densities. Pressure altitude is the indicated altitude when the altimeter is set to 29.92 (the standard datum plane). Density altitude is pressure altitude adjusted for nonstandard temperature.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Cabin altitude is the altitude that corresponds to the pressure within the cabin of a pressurized airplane. Answer (C) is incorrect. True altitude is the height above sea level. Airport, terrain, and obstacle elevations found on aeronautical charts are true altitudes.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 이륙·상승·순항·착륙 성능표는 기압고도와 밀도고도를 기준으로 한다. 기압고도는 29.92 inHg 설정에서의 지시고도이고, 밀도고도는 여기에 비표준 온도를 보정한 값이다.

question: Density altitude is the vertical distance above mean sea level in the standard atmosphere at which

choices.A: pressure altitude is corrected for standard temperature.
choices.B: a given atmospheric density is to be found.
choices.C: temperature, pressure, altitude, and humidity are considered.

explanation.en:
Density altitude is defined as the vertical distance above mean sea level at which a given atmospheric density is to be found.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Density altitude is pressure altitude corrected for nonstandard temperature, not standard temperature. Answer (C) is incorrect. Temperature, pressure, altitude, and humidity all can affect density altitude, but they do not define density altitude.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 밀도고도는 실제 공기밀도와 같은 밀도를 갖는 표준대기상의 고도이다.

question: To determine pressure altitude prior to takeoff, the altimeter should be set to

choices.A: the current altimeter setting.
choices.B: 29.92" Hg and the altimeter indication noted.
choices.C: the field elevation and the pressure reading in the altimeter setting window noted.

explanation.en:
Pressure altitude can be determined by either of two methods: (1) Set the barometric scale of the altimeter to 29.92 and read the indicated altitude, or (2) apply a correction factor to the airport elevation according to the reported altimeter setting.

Answer (A) is incorrect. With the current altimeter setting in the altimeter, the altimeter should indicate the airport elevation (i.e., true altitude), not pressure altitude. Answer (C) is incorrect. The pressure reading in the altimeter setting window should be the current altimeter setting, which should indicate the airport elevation (i.e., true, not pressure, altitude).

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 고도계를 29.92 inHg로 설정한 뒤 읽은 고도가 기압고도이다. 또는 현재 고도계 설정값을 이용해 공항 표고에 보정치를 적용한다.

question: At higher elevation airports the pilot should know that indicated airspeed

choices.A: will be unchanged, but groundspeed will be faster.
choices.B: will be higher, but groundspeed will be unchanged.
choices.C: should be increased to compensate for the thinner air.

explanation.en:
If an airplane of given weight and configuration is operated at greater heights above standard sea level, the airplane will still require the same dynamic pressure to become airborne at the takeoff lift coefficient. Thus, the airplane at altitude will take off at the same indicated airspeed as at sea level, but because of the reduced air density, the true airspeed (and groundspeed) will be greater.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The indicated airspeed will remain the same, not higher, and the groundspeed will be higher, not unchanged. Answer (C) is incorrect. The true, not indicated, airspeed will increase at higher elevation airports due to the thinner (i.e., reduced air density) air.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 11)
explanation.kr: 같은 중량·형상에서는 고지대 공항에서도 비슷한 지시대기속도로 이륙한다. 공기밀도가 낮으므로 해당 진대기속도와 무풍 지상속도는 더 높다.

question: As air temperature increases, density altitude will

choices.A: decrease.
choices.B: increase.
choices.C: remain the same.

explanation.en:
Increasing the temperature of a substance decreases its density, and a decrease in air density means a higher density altitude. Thus, with an increase in temperature, the air density decreases, providing a higher density altitude.

Answer (A) is incorrect. As temperature increases, the density altitude will increase, not decrease. Answer (C) is incorrect. Density varies inversely with temperature. Increasing the temperature of a substance decreases its density, and a decrease in air density means a higher density altitude.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 4)
explanation.kr: 기온이 높아지면 공기밀도는 감소한다. 더 낮은 밀도는 더 높은 밀도고도를 뜻한다.

question: What effect does an uphill runway slope have on takeoff performance?

choices.A: Increases takeoff speed.
choices.B: Increases takeoff distance.
choices.C: Decreases takeoff distance.

explanation.en:
The upslope or downslope of the runway (runway gradient) is quite important when runway length and takeoff distance are critical. Upslope provides a retarding force that impedes acceleration because the engine has to overcome gravity as well as surface friction and drag, resulting in a longer ground run or takeoff.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The indicated takeoff speed is the same on a level, downhill, or uphill runway at a given density altitude. Answer (C) is incorrect. A downhill, not an uphill, runway slope will decrease the takeoff distance.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 11)
explanation.kr: 오르막 활주로에서는 마찰·항력뿐 아니라 중력의 경사방향 성분도 이겨야 한다. 가속이 늦어져 이륙 활주거리가 늘어난다.

question:
Which maximum range factor decreases as
weight decreases?

choices.A: Altitude.
choices.B: Airspeed.
choices.C: Angle of attack.

explanation.en:
As weight decreases, the maximum range is achieved when the airplane is flown at the airspeed which maximizes the lift/drag ratio. As weight decreases, the L/DMAX airspeed decreases.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Maximum range altitude may increase, not decrease, with weight decrease. Answer (C) is incorrect. Angle of attack is not a maximum range factor (as are weight, altitude, and power setting).

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 11)
explanation.kr: 중량이 줄면 최대 양항비를 얻는 속도도 낮아진다. 따라서 최대 항속거리에 대응하는 최적 속도는 감소한다.

question:
When computing weight and balance, the basic
empty weight includes the weight of the airframe,
engine(s), and all installed optional equipment. Basic
empty weight also includes

choices.A: the unusable fuel, full operating fluids, and full oil.
choices.B: all usable fuel, full oil, hydraulic fluid, but does not include the weight of pilot, passengers, or baggage.
choices.C: all usable fuel and oil, but does not include any radio equipment or instruments that were installed by someone other than the manufacturer.

explanation.en:
Empty weight consists of the airframe, the engine, and all installed optional equipment, including fixed ballast, unusable fuel, full operating fluids, and full oil.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Empty weight does not include usable fuel. Answer (C) is incorrect. Empty weight does not include usable fuel, but it does include all installed equipment.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 10)
explanation.kr: 기본공허중량에는 기체·엔진·장착 장비와 고정 밸러스트, 사용불가 연료, 정상 작동유체 및 전량의 오일이 포함된다.

question: The CG of an aircraft can be determined by which of the following methods?

choices.A: Dividing total arms by total moments.
choices.B: Multiplying total arms by total weight.
choices.C: Dividing total moments by total weight.

explanation.en:
The center of gravity, by definition, is the total moment of the airplane divided by its total weight. Moment is the position of weight from some fixed point (called the datum) multiplied by that weight.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Arms are the distances of weight from the datum; each arm is individually multiplied by its respective weight to determine an individual moment.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Arms are the distances of weight from the datum; each arm is individually multiplied by its respective weight to determine an individual moment.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 10)
explanation.kr: 각 항목의 모멘트는 중량×기준면으로부터의 거리이다. 항공기 무게중심은 총모멘트를 총중량으로 나눠 구한다.

question: The CG of an aircraft may be determined by

choices.A: dividing total arms by total moments.
choices.B: dividing total moments by total weight.
choices.C: multiplying total weight by total moments.

explanation.en:
The center of gravity, by definition, is the total moment of the airplane divided by its total weight. Moment is the position of weight from some fixed point (called the datum) multiplied by that weight.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Arms are the distances of weight from the datum; each arm is individually multiplied by its respective weight to determine an individual moment.

Answer (C) is incorrect. You must divide total moments by total weight (not vice versa).

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 10)
explanation.kr: 무게중심 CG=총모멘트÷총중량이다. 각 모멘트는 해당 중량과 모멘트팔을 곱한 값이다.

question:
If all index units are positive when computing
weight and balance, the location of the datum would
be at the

choices.A: centerline of the main wheels.
choices.B: nose, or out in front of the airplane.
choices.C: centerline of the nose or tailwheel, depending on the type of airplane.

explanation.en:
Index units refer to arms. If all the arms are positive in computing weight and balance, the datum (or starting point) must be at the nose or out in front of the nose of the airplane. If it is somewhere between the nose and the tail, some items (those between the datum and the nose) would be negative.

Answer (A) is incorrect. If the datum were at the centerline of the main wheels, the engine would have a negative arm (or index unit). Answer (C) is incorrect. If the datum were at the centerline of the nose or tailwheel, at least the propeller would have a negative arm (or index unit).

Source: (FAA-H-8083-1B Chap 2)
explanation.kr: 모든 모멘트팔이 양수라면 기준면은 기수 또는 그보다 앞에 있어야 한다. 기준면 뒤쪽에 있는 물체의 팔이 양수로 계산되기 때문이다.

question:
GIVEN:
Weight A -- 155 pounds at 45 inches aft of datum
Weight B -- 165 pounds at 145 inches aft of datum
Weight C -- 95 pounds at 185 inches aft of datum
Based on this information, where would the CG be
located aft of datum?

choices.A: 86.0 inches.
choices.B: 116.8 inches.
choices.C: 125.0 inches.

explanation.en:
Multiply each weight by its arm: 155 × 45 = 6,975; 165 × 145 = 23,925; 95 × 185 = 17,575 lb·in. Total weight = 415 lb; total moment = 48,475 lb·in. CG = total moment / total weight = 48,475 / 415 ≈ 116.8 in aft of datum.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The CG is 116.8 in. , not 86.0 in.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The CG is 116.8 in., not 125.0 in.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-1B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 각 모멘트를 합하면 48,475 lb·in, 중량 합계는 415 lb이다. CG=48,475÷415≈116.8 in로 기준면 뒤에 위치한다.

question:
GIVEN:
Weight A -- 140 pounds at 17 inches aft of datum
Weight B -- 120 pounds at 110 inches aft of datum
Weight C -- 85 pounds at 210 inches aft of datum
Based on this information, the CG would be located
how far aft of datum?

choices.A: 89.11 inches.
choices.B: 96.89 inches.
choices.C: 106.92 inches.

explanation.en:
Individual moments are 140 × 17 = 2,380; 120 × 110 = 13,200; and 85 × 210 = 17,850 lb·in. Total weight = 345 lb and total moment = 33,430 lb·in. CG = 33,430 / 345 ≈ 96.89 in aft of datum.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The CG is 96.89 in., not 89.11 in.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The CG is 96.89 in., not 106.92 in.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-1B Chap 5)

question:
GIVEN:
WEIGHT ARM MOMENT
Empty weight 957 29.07 ?
Pilot (fwd seat) 140 -45.30 ?
Passenger (aft seat) 170 +1.60 ?
Ballast 15 -45.30 ?
TOTALS ? ? ?
The CG is located at station

explanation.en:
Individual moments are 957 × 29.07 = 27,819.99; 140 × (-45.30) = -6,342.00; 170 × 1.60 = 272.00; and 15 × (-45.30) = -679.50 lb·in. Total weight = 1,282 lb; total moment = 21,070.49 lb·in. CG = 21,070.49 / 1,282 ≈ +16.43.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The CG is +16.43, not-6.43.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The CG is +16.43, not +27.38.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-1B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 각 항목의 중량×팔을 합하면 총모멘트 21,070.49 lb·in, 총중량 1,282 lb이다. CG=21,070.49÷1,282≈+16.43이다.

question:
GIVEN:
Weight A -- 135 pounds at 15 inches aft of datum
Weight B -- 205 pounds at 117 inches aft of datum
Weight C -- 85 pounds at 195 inches aft of datum
Based on this information, the CG would be located
how far aft of datum?

choices.A: 100.2 inches.
choices.B: 109.0 inches.
choices.C: 121.7inches.

explanation.en:
Individual moments are 135 × 15 = 2,025; 205 × 117 = 23,985; and 85 × 195 = 16,575 lb·in. Total weight = 425 lb; total moment = 42,585 lb·in. CG = 42,585 / 425 = 100.2 in aft of datum.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The CG is 100.2 in., not 109.0 in.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The CG is 100.2 in., not 121.7 in.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-1B Chap 5)

question:
GIVEN:
Weight A -- 175 pounds at 135 inches aft of datum
Weight B -- 135 pounds at 115 inches aft of datum
Weight C -- 75 pounds at 85 inches aft of datum
The CG for the combined weights would be located
how far aft of datum?

choices.A: 91.76 inches.
choices.B: 111.67 inches.
choices.C: 118.24 inches.

explanation.en:
Individual moments are 175 × 135 = 23,625; 135 × 115 = 15,525; and 75 × 85 = 6,375 lb·in. Total weight = 385 lb; total moment = 45,525 lb·in. CG = 45,525 / 385 ≈ 118.24 in aft of datum.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The CG is 118.24 in., not 91.76 in. Answer (B) is incorrect. The CG is 118.24 in., not 111.67 in.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-1B Chap 5)
explanation.kr: 총모멘트 45,525 lb·in을 총중량 385 lb로 나눈다. CG≈118.24 in로 기준면 뒤에 위치한다.

question:
GIVEN:
Total weight 4,137 lb
CG location Station 67.8
Fuel consumption 13.7 GPH
Fuel CG Station 68.0
After 1 hour 30 minutes of flight time, the CG would
be located at station

explanation.en:
Fuel weight consumed = 13.7 gal/hr × 1.5 hr × 6 lb/gal = 123.3 lb. New CG = (original moment - fuel moment) / (original weight - fuel weight) = [(4,137 × 67.8) - (123.3 × 68.0)] / (4,137 - 123.3) = 272,104.2 / 4,013.7 ≈ 67.79.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The new CG is 67.79, not 68.79.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The new CG is 67.79, not 70.78.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-1B Chap 2)

question:
GIVEN:
Total weight 3,037 lb
CG location Station 68.8
Fuel consumption 12.7 GPH
Fuel CG Station 68.0
After 1 hour 45 minutes of flight time, the CG would
be located at station

explanation.en:
Fuel weight consumed = 12.7 gal/hr × 1.75 hr × 6 lb/gal = 133.35 lb. New CG = [(3,037 × 68.8) - (133.35 × 68.0)] / (3,037 - 133.35) = 199,877.8 / 2,903.65 ≈ 68.83.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The new CG is 68.83, not 68.77.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The new CG is 68.83, not 69.77.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-1B Chap 2)

question:
An airplane is loaded to a gross weight of
4,800 pounds, with three pieces of luggage in the
rear baggage compartment. The CG is located
98 inches aft of datum, which is 1 inch aft of limits. If
luggage which weighs 90 pounds is moved from the
rear baggage compartment (145 inches aft of datum)
to the front compartment (45 inches aft of datum),
what is the new CG?

choices.A: 96.13 inches aft of datum.
choices.B: 95.50 inches aft of datum.
choices.C: 99.87 inches aft of datum.

explanation.en:
Moving baggage within the airplane does not change total weight. The forward shift reduces moment by 90 × (145 - 45) = 9,000 lb·in. New CG = [(4,800 × 98) - 9,000] / 4,800 = 461,400 / 4,800 ≈ 96.13.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The new CG is 96.13, not 95.50.

Answer (C) is incorrect. The new CG is 96.13, not 99.87.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-1B Chap 2)
explanation.kr: 90 lb의 짐을 100 in 앞으로 옮기면 모멘트가 9,000 lb·in 감소한다. 총중량은 그대로이므로 새 CG=(4,800×98-9,000)÷4,800≈96.13이다.

question:
An aircraft is loaded with a ramp weight
of 3,650 pounds and having a CG of 94.0,
approximately how much baggage would have to be
moved from the rear baggage area at station 180 to
the forward baggage area at station 40 in order to
move the CG to 92.0?

choices.A: 52.14 pounds.
choices.B: 62.24 pounds.
choices.C: 78.14 pounds.

explanation.en:
Total weight is unchanged. Required moment reduction = 3,650 × (94.0 - 92.0) = 7,300 lb·in. The baggage moves forward by 180 - 40 = 140 in. Required baggage weight = 7,300 / 140 ≈ 52.14 lb.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Only 52.14 lb., not 62.24 lb., of baggage needs to be shifted. Answer (C) is incorrect. Only 52.14 lb., not 78.14 lb., of baggage needs to be shifted.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-1B Chap 2)
explanation.kr: 필요한 모멘트 감소량은 3,650×(94-92)=7,300 lb·in이다. 이동거리 180-40=140 in로 나누면 앞으로 옮길 짐은 약 52.14 lb이다.

question: Which is not a type of hypoxia?

choices.A: Histotoxic.
choices.B: Hypoxic.
choices.C: Hypertoxic.

explanation.en:
There is no such thing as hypertoxic hypoxia. The four types of hypoxia are histotoxic, hypoxic, anemic (hypemic), and stagnant hypoxia.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The four types of hypoxia are histotoxic, hypoxic, anemic (hypemic), and stagnant hypoxia.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The four types of hypoxia are histotoxic, hypoxic, anemic (hypemic), and stagnant hypoxia.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 저산소증은 저산소성·빈혈성·정체성·조직독성의 네 종류로 구분한다. Hypertoxic hypoxia는 이 분류에 해당하지 않는다.

question: Which of the following is a correct response to counteract the feelings of hypoxia in flight?

choices.A: Promptly descend to a lower altitude.
choices.B: Increase cabin air flow.
choices.C: Avoid sudden inhalations.

explanation.en:
The correct response to counteract feelings of hypoxia is to descend to a lower altitude or use supplemental oxygen, if the aircraft is so equipped.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Increasing the amount of air flowing inside an aircraft will not help counteract hypoxia. Because of the reduction of partial pressure at higher altitudes, there is less oxygen in the air to draw from. Answer (C) is incorrect. Breathing deeply or suddenly will not counteract feelings of hypoxia.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 비행 중 저산소증 증상이 의심되면 더 낮은 고도로 내려가거나, 장비가 있으면 보조산소를 사용한다.

question: Hypoxia susceptibility due to inhalation of carbon monoxide increases as

choices.A: altitude increases.
choices.B: humidity decreases.
choices.C: oxygen demand increases.

explanation.en:
The inhalation of carbon monoxide reduces body's ability to transport oxygen. The red blood cells will pick up carbon monoxide molecules instead of oxygen. This problem is compounded by increasing altitude, which also limits the body's ability to transport oxygen.

Answer (B) is incorrect. A change in humidity does not change the body's susceptibility to hypoxia due to the inhalation of carbon monoxide. Answer (C) is incorrect. An increase in altitude, not an increase in oxygen demand, increases the susceptibility to hypoxia when carbon monoxide is inhaled.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 일산화탄소는 혈액의 산소 운반을 방해한다. 고도가 높아지면 산소 공급 여건도 나빠져 저산소증에 더 취약해진다.

question: Altitude-induced hypoxia is caused by what atmospheric condition?

choices.A: Significantly less oxygen molecules at high altitude.
choices.B: Insufficient partial pressure of the inhaled oxygen.
choices.C: Incorrect balance of oxygen and carbon dioxide.

explanation.en:
As altitude is increased, the partial pressure of oxygen lowers, reducing the lungs' capacity to effectively transfer oxygen from the ambient air to the blood to be carried to the tissues of the body.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The percentage of oxygen does not change at higher altitudes, though the molecules of oxygen in ambient air get further apart, exerting less pressure per square inch. Answer (C) is incorrect. An incorrect balance of oxygen and carbon dioxide is primarily associated with hyperventilation.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-2)
explanation.kr: 고도 상승으로 산소 분압이 낮아지면 폐에서 혈액으로 산소를 전달하기 어려워진다. 이것이 고도에 따른 저산소증의 원인이다.

question: Dry ice sublimates (solid to gas) into large quantities of C02 gas, which can rapidly displace oxygen containing air and cause which type of hypoxia?

choices.A: Hypoxic.
choices.B: Hypemic.
choices.C: Histotoxic.

explanation.en:
Dry ice sublimates into large quantities of C02 gas, which can rapidly displace oxygen containing air and cause hypoxia via carbon dioxide intoxication. Case studies have shown that both illness and death can be caused by exposure when transporting dry ice in small, confined spaces such as a flight deck or cabin. Exposure to a high concentration of C02 gas can lead to increased respiration, tachycardia, cardiac arrhythmia, and unconsciousness. Exposure to a concentration of C02 gas in excess of 10% can cause convulsions, coma, and/or death.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Anemic (hypemic) hypoxia occurs when blood is not able to take up and transport a sufficient amount of oxygen to the cells in the body. Answer (C) is incorrect. Histotoxic hypoxia is the inability of cells to effectively use oxygen.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 드라이아이스가 승화하면 많은 CO2가 발생해 산소를 포함한 공기를 밀어낼 수 있다. 좁은 조종실·객실에서는 CO2 중독과 저산소증이 생길 수 있으며, 고농도는 의식소실 등 심각한 결과를 초래한다.

question: If a pilot has not consumed a drink in 12 hours, and has a blood alcohol level of 0.04 percent, can they fly?

choices.A: Yes, if it has been in excess of 8 hours since the pilot last consumed alcohol.
choices.B: No, the pilot has a blood alcohol level of 0.04.
choices.C: Yes, the FAA requires at least 12 hours and a blood alcohol level of 0.04.

explanation.en:
Pilots are required to have a blood alcohol level that is less than 0.04%, and at least 8 hours must have passed since the last alcoholic beverage was consumed.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The FAA requires pilots to wait at least 8 hours from the time an alcoholic beverage is consumed to the time flight is attempted. In addition to the minimum of 8 hours, pilots must also have a blood alcohol level that is less than 0.04%. Answer (C) is incorrect. The FAA requires that at least 8 hours pass between the last consumption of alcohol and the beginning of a flight. Further, the blood alcohol level must be less than 0.04%.

Source: (14 CFR 91.17)
explanation.kr: 원문의 미국 기준은 마지막 음주 후 최소 8시간과 혈중알코올농도 0.04% 미만을 모두 요구한다. 12시간이 지났더라도 0.04%라면 기준을 충족하지 못한다.

question: 14 CFR 91.17 requires that blood alcohol level be less than

choices.A: 0.40% when piloting an aircraft.
choices.B: 0.08% when piloting an aircraft.
choices.C: 0.04% when piloting an aircraft.

explanation.en:
Current regulations require that a pilot's blood alcohol level be less than 0.04% and that a minimum of 8 hours passes between consuming alcohol and piloting an aircraft.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Pilots should have a blood alcohol level of less than 0.04%, not 0.40%. Answer (B) is incorrect. Pilots should have a blood alcohol level of less than 0.04%, not 0.08%.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 원문이 인용한 14 CFR 91.17 기준은 혈중알코올농도 0.04% 미만과 마지막 음주 후 최소 8시간 경과이다.

question: According to current regulations, how many hours must elapse between consuming alcohol and piloting an aircraft?

choices.A: 4 hours.
choices.B: 8 hours.
choices.C: 16 hours.

explanation.en:
According to 14 CFR 91.17, a minimum of 8 hours must pass between consuming alcohol and flying an aircraft.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Regulations require that a minimum of 8 hours, not 4 hours, must pass between consuming alcohol and flying an aircraft. Answer (C) is incorrect. While considerable amounts of alcohol may remain in the body for over 16 hours, and it is good to be cautious about flying too soon after drinking, the regulations state that a minimum of 8 hours must elapse between consuming alcohol and flying.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 원문 기준 음주 후 조종까지 최소 8시간이 지나야 한다. 시간 경과 외에 알코올의 영향과 혈중농도 요건도 충족해야 한다.

question: Which of the following statements concerning the combination of alcohol and altitude is true?

choices.A: Judgment and decision-making abilities will only be affected at altitudes greater than 2,000 ft. MSL.
choices.B: Altitude multiplies the effects of alcohol.
choices.C: Increases in altitude do not change how alcohol affects individuals.

explanation.en:
Altitude multiplies the effects of alcohol on the brain; at higher altitudes, alcohol from two drinks may have the same effect as three or four drinks at lower altitudes.

Answer (A) is incorrect. An increase in altitude, no matter how small, can multiply the effects of alcohol on the body.

Answer (C) is incorrect. Increasing altitude multiplies the effects alcohol will have on the body.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 고도는 알코올이 뇌에 미치는 영향을 악화시킨다. 원문은 높은 고도에서 같은 음주량도 더 큰 기능 저하를 일으킬 수 있다고 설명한다.

question: Hypoxia is the result of which of these conditions?

choices.A: Excessive oxygen in the bloodstream.
choices.B: Insufficient oxygen reaching the brain.
choices.C: Excessive carbon dioxide in the bloodstream.

explanation.en:
Hypoxia is a state of oxygen deficiency in the bloodstream sufficient to impair function of the brain and other organs.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The problem is insufficient oxygen, not excessive oxygen. Answer (C) is incorrect. It is a nonsense answer. Insufficient, not excessive, carbon dioxide in the bloodstream is the result of hyperventilation, not hypoxia.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-2)
explanation.kr: 저산소증은 뇌와 다른 장기의 기능을 떨어뜨릴 정도로 산소 공급이 부족해진 상태이다.

question: To rid itself of the alcohol contained in one mixed drink, the human body requires about

choices.A: 1 hour.
choices.B: 2 hours.
choices.C: 3 hours.

explanation.en:
The body requires about 3 hours to rid itself of all the alcohol contained in one mixed drink, one beer, or one glass of wine.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The body requires 3 hours, not 1 hour, to rid itself of all the alcohol contained in one mixed drink, one beer, or one glass of wine. Answer (B) is incorrect. The body requires 3 hours, not 2 hours, to rid itself of all the alcohol contained in one mixed drink, one beer, or one glass of wine.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 원문은 칵테일·맥주·와인 한 잔의 알코올을 몸에서 제거하는 데 약 3시간이 걸린다고 설명한다. 이 수치는 책의 학습용 설명이며 개인별 비행 적합성 판단 기준과는 구분한다.

question: Which is true regarding the presence of alcohol within the human body?

choices.A: A small amount of alcohol increases vision acuity.
choices.B: An increase in altitude decreases the adverse effect of alcohol.
choices.C: Judgment and decision-making abilities can be adversely affected by even small amounts of alcohol.

explanation.en:
As little as 1 ounce of liquor, 12 ounces of beer, or 4 ounces (one glass) of wine can impair flying skills, with the alcohol consumed in these drinks being detectable in the breath and blood for at least 3 hr.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Any amount of alcohol decreases, not increases, virtually all mental and physical activities.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Increases in altitude increase, not decrease, the adverse effects of alcohol.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-1)
explanation.kr: 적은 양의 주류도 비행 능력을 저하시킬 수 있다. 원문은 주류의 알코올이 호흡과 혈액에서 최소 약 3시간 검출될 수 있다고 설명한다.

question: With a blood alcohol level below 0.04 percent, a pilot cannot fly sooner than

choices.A: 4 hours after drinking alcohol.
choices.B: 12 hours after drinking alcohol.
choices.C: 8 hours after drinking alcohol.

explanation.en:
According to 14 CFR 91.17, a minimum of 8 hours must pass between consuming alcohol and flying an aircraft.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A pilot who has consumed alcohol must wait more than 4 hours before flying. Answer (B) is incorrect. While considerable amounts of alcohol may remain in the body for over 12 hours and it is good to be cautious about flying too soon after drinking, the regulations state that a minimum of 8 hours must elapse between consuming alcohol and flying.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 혈중알코올농도가 0.04% 미만이더라도 마지막 음주 후 최소 8시간이라는 원문의 대기시간 요건을 충족해야 한다.

question: You attended a party last night and you consumed several glasses of wine. You are planning to fly your aircraft home and have been careful to make sure 8 hours have passed since your last alcoholic drink. You can make the flight now only if you are not under the influence of alcohol and your blood alcohol level is

choices.A: below 0.04%.
choices.B: below 0.08%.

explanation.en:
14 CFR Part 91 requires that blood alcohol level be less than 0.04% and that a minimum of 8 hr. passes between drinking alcohol and piloting an aircraft. A pilot with a blood alcohol level of 0.04% or greater after 8 hr. cannot fly until his or her blood alcohol level falls below that amount. Even though the blood alcohol level may be well below 0.04%, a pilot cannot fly sooner than the minimum of 8 hr. after drinking alcohol.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The legal limit for motor vehicle operation in many states is 0.08%. However, to operate an aircraft, a pilot's blood alcohol level must be below 0.04% and a minimum of 8 hr. must have passed since consuming the last drink. Answer (C) is incorrect. The legal limit to operate an aircraft is 0.04%. With a blood alcohol level of 0.0%, a pilot would be legally able to fly as long as it has been more than the minimum of 8 hr. since his or her last alcoholic beverage.

Source: (14 CFR 91.17)
explanation.kr: 8시간이 지났다는 사실만으로 비행할 수 있는 것은 아니다. 원문 기준 알코올의 영향이 없어야 하고 혈중알코올농도도 0.04% 미만이어야 한다.

question: Which of the following could increase susceptibility to hypoxia?

choices.A: Breathing 100% oxygen at too low of an altitude.
choices.B: Rapidly descending from a high altitude.
choices.C: Flying after donating blood.

explanation.en:
Anemic hypoxia can be caused by a loss of blood, such as after a blood donation. Blood volume can require several weeks to return to normal following a donation. Although the effects of the blood loss are minimal at ground level, there are risks when flying during this time.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Hypoxia occurs due tp a lack of oxygen, so breathing 100% oxygen would not increase susceptibility to hypoxia. Answer (B) is incorrect. Descending to a lower altitude increases the amount of breathable oxygen, so this would not increase susceptibility to hypoxia.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 헌혈로 혈액량과 산소 운반 능력이 줄면 빈혈성 저산소증에 취약해질 수 있다. 지상에서 증상이 적어도 고도에서는 위험이 커질 수 있다고 원문은 설명한다.

question: A pilot making a blood donation in order to help a sick associate should be aware that for several weeks

choices.A: sufficient oxygen may not reach the cells in the body.
choices.B: fewer oxygen molecules will be available to the respiratory membranes.
choices.C: the ability of the body tissues to effectively use oxygen is decreased.

explanation.en:
Blood donations can cause anemic hypoxia because not enough blood is available to carry a sufficient amount of oxygen to the cells.

Answer (B) is incorrect. The amount of oxygen available to the body does not change; however, there may not be enough blood to carry the oxygen to the cells. Answer (C) is incorrect. The body tissues have not lost the ability to use oxygen; however, the amount of blood available to deliver the oxygen has decreased.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 헌혈 후에는 조직으로 산소를 운반하는 능력이 감소할 수 있다. 원문은 수주간 빈혈성 저산소증에 대한 주의가 필요하다고 설명한다.

question: To rid itself of all the alcohol contained in one beer, the human body requires about

choices.A: 1 hour.
choices.B: 4 hours.
choices.C: 3 hours.

explanation.en:
The body requires about 3 hours to rid itself of all the alcohol contained in one mixed drink, one beer, or one glass of wine.

Answer (A) is incorrect. The body requires 3 hours, not 1 hour, to rid itself of all the alcohol contained in one mixed drink, one beer, or one glass of wine. Answer (B) is incorrect. The body requires 3 hours, not 4 hours, to rid itself of all the alcohol contained in one mixed drink, one beer, or one glass of wine.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 원문은 맥주 한 잔에 포함된 알코올을 모두 제거하는 데 약 3시간이 걸린다고 제시한다. 개인별 회복시간이나 비행 가능 여부를 보장하는 수치는 아니다.

question: While experiencing a hangover, a pilot

choices.A: will have impaired motor and mental responses.
choices.B: is no longer under the influence of alcohol.
choices.C: may experience discomfort, but no impairment.

explanation.en:
While experiencing a hangover, a pilot is still under the influence of alcohol. Although a pilot may think they are functioning normally, motor and mental response impairment is still present.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Considerable amounts of alcohol can remain in the body for over 16 hours, and the effects and symptoms of a hangover are because of the influence of alcohol. Answer (C) is incorrect. Although a pilot may think they are functioning normally, motor and mental response impairment is still present.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 숙취가 있으면 알코올의 영향이 남아 있는 상태이다. 스스로 정상이라고 느껴도 운동·정신 반응 능력은 저하되어 있을 수 있다.

question: Which of the following common over-the-counter (OTC) drugs can cause noticeable adverse side effects, including drowsiness and cognitive deficits?

choices.A: Acetaminophen and ibuprofen.
choices.B: Diphenhydramine.
choices.C: Acetylsalicylic acid.

explanation.en:
Some common OTC drugs, for example, antihistamines and decongestants, can cause noticeable adverse side effects, including drowsiness and cognitive deficits. The symptoms associated with common upper respiratory infections, including the common cold, often suppress a pilot's desire to fly, and treating symptoms with a drug that has adverse side effects only compounds the problem. Particularly, medications containing diphenhydramine (e.g., Benadryl) are known to cause drowsiness and have a prolonged half-life, meaning the drugs stay in the system for an extended time, which lengthens the time that side effects are present.

Answer (A) is incorrect. OTC analgesics, such as acetaminophen (e.g., Tylenol) and ibuprofen (e.g., Advil), have few side effects when taken in the correct dosage.

Answer (C) is incorrect. Acetylsalicylic acid (i.e., aspirin) is an OTC analgesic with few side effects when taken in the correct dosage.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 디펜히드라민이 든 일반의약품은 졸림과 인지기능 저하를 일으킬 수 있다. 반감기가 길어 부작용이 오래 지속될 수 있다고 원문은 설명한다.

question: Which is a common symptom of hyperventilation?

choices.A: Drowsiness.
choices.B: Decreased breathing rate.
choices.C: Euphoria - sense of well-being.

explanation.en:
Hyperventilation is an abnormal increase in breathing, which can occur subconsciously when a stressful situation is encountered. It can cause lightheadedness, drowsiness, suffocation, tingling in the extremities, and coolness.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Hyperventilation usually occurs from an increased, not a decreased, breathing rate. Answer (C) is incorrect. Euphoria is a potential symptom of hypoxia, not hyperventilation.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-3)
explanation.kr: 과호흡은 스트레스 상황에서 무의식적으로 호흡량이 증가하는 현상이다. 어지러움·졸림·질식감·사지 저림·차가운 느낌 등이 나타날 수 있다.

question: To overcome the symptoms of hyperventilation, a pilot should

choices.A: swallow or yawn.
choices.B: slow the breathing rate.
choices.C: increase the breathing rate.

explanation.en:
A pilot should be able to overcome the symptoms of hyperventilation by slowing the breathing rate or breathing into a bag.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Swallowing or yawning helps to equalize ear pressures, not overcome hyperventilation.

Answer (C) is incorrect. Increasing the breathing rate aggravates hyperventilation.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-3)
explanation.kr: 과호흡 증상에 대한 원문의 핵심 대처는 호흡 속도를 늦추는 것이다. 과도한 호흡으로 이산화탄소가 빠져나가는 상태를 줄이기 위한 조치이다.

question: As hyperventilation progresses a pilot can experience

choices.A: decreased breathing rate and depth.
choices.B: heightened awareness and feeling of wellbeing.
choices.C: symptoms of suffocation and drowsiness.

explanation.en:
Hyperventilation is an abnormal increase in breathing, which can occur subconsciously when a stressful situation is encountered. It can cause lightheadedness, drowsiness, suffocation, tingling in the extremities, and coolness.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Hyperventilation is an increase, not a decrease, of the breathing rate and depth. Answer (B) is incorrect. Heightened awareness and euphoria are potential symptoms of hypoxia, not hyperventilation.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-3)
explanation.kr: 과호흡이 진행되면 어지러움, 졸림, 질식감, 팔다리 저림과 냉감 등이 나타날 수 있다.

question: Which would most likely result in hyperventilation?

choices.A: Insufficient oxygen.
choices.B: Excessive carbon monoxide.
choices.C: Insufficient carbon dioxide.

explanation.en:
Hyperventilation occurs when an excessive amount of carbon dioxide is passed out of the body and too much oxygen is retained.

Answer (A) is incorrect. It describes hypoxia. Answer (B) is incorrect. It describes carbon monoxide poisoning.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-3)
explanation.kr: 과호흡에서는 호흡량이 과도해 이산화탄소가 지나치게 배출된다. 핵심은 산소 부족과 혼동하기 쉬운 증상이 나타날 수 있다는 점이다.

question: Which is a common symptom of hyperventilation?

choices.A: Tingling sensations.
choices.B: Visual acuity.
choices.C: Decreased breathing rate.

explanation.en:
Hyperventilation results from an abnormal increase in the volume of air breathed in and out of the lungs. It can occur subconsciously when a stressful situation is encountered. The result is an excessive amount of carbon dioxide removed from the body. The symptoms are lightheadedness, suffocation, drowsiness, tingling of the extremities, and coolness.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Hyperventilation distorts one's abilities; it does not improve them. Answer (C) is incorrect. Decreasing the breathing rate is one way to overcome hyperventilation. It is not a symptom of it.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-3)
explanation.kr: 스트레스로 호흡량이 비정상적으로 늘면 CO2가 과도하게 제거된다. 그 결과 어지러움·질식감·졸림·사지 저림·냉감이 생길 수 있다.

question: Which of the following flight conditions would indicate a pilot is experiencing spatial disorientation?

choices.A: Steep turn.
choices.B: Graveyard spiral.
choices.C: Turns around a point.

explanation.en:
A graveyard spiral is an example of a pilot being adversely affected by spatial disorientation.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Steep turns are common maneuvers performed during training and do not indicate that a pilot is experiencing spatial disorientation. Answer (C) is incorrect. Turns around a point are maneuvers performed during training and do not indicate that a pilot is experiencing spatial disorientation.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 무덤 나선강하 Graveyard spiral는 공간정위상실의 대표적인 사례이다.

question: A state of temporary confusion resulting from misleading information being sent to the brain by various sensory organs is defined as

choices.A: spatial disorientation.
choices.B: hyperventilation.
choices.C: hypoxia.

explanation.en:
A state of temporary confusion resulting from misleading information being sent to the brain by various sensory organs is defined as vertigo (spatial disorientation). Put simply, the pilot cannot determine his or her relationship to the earth's horizon.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Hyperventilation causes excessive oxygen and/or a decrease in carbon dioxide in the bloodstream. Answer (C) is incorrect. Hypoxia occurs when there is insufficient oxygen in the bloodstream.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-5)
explanation.kr: 감각기관이 뇌에 잘못된 정보를 보내 자신의 자세와 지평선의 관계를 판단하지 못하는 상태가 공간정위상실이다.

question: How may a pilot overcome spatial disorientation?

choices.A: By relying on his flight instruments.
choices.B: By decreasing the amount of time spent looking inside.
choices.C: By relying on all outside visual references.

explanation.en:
Ways to overcome the effects of spatial disorientation include relying on the airplane instruments, avoiding sudden head movements, and ensuring that outside visual references are fixed points on the surface.

Answer (B) is incorrect. Decreasing the amount of time spent looking inside is not a remedy for overcoming spatial disorientation. Answer (C) is incorrect. Not all visual references can be relied on, as some may be moving. A pilot must ensure that any outside visual references are fixed points on the surface.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 공간정위상실을 극복하려면 비행계기를 신뢰하고 갑작스러운 머리 움직임을 피한다. 외부 시각 기준을 사용할 때는 지표의 고정된 지점을 이용한다.

question: You are most likely to experience somatogravic illusion during

choices.A: a rapid descent.
choices.B: deceleration upon landing.
choices.C: rapid acceleration on takeoff.

explanation.en:
A rapid acceleration, such as one experienced during takeoff, stimulates the otolith organs (in the inner ear) in the same way as tilting the head backwards. This action may create what is known as the somatogravic illusion of being in a nose-up attitude, especially in conditions with poor visual references.

Answer (A) is incorrect. A rapid acceleration, not a rapid descent, stimulates the otolith organs in the same way as tilting the head backwards, which is a common experience of · somatogravic illusion. Answer (B) is incorrect. During landing, a rapid deceleration may cause somatogravic illusion with the opposite effect of a rapid acceleration. However, a normal deceleration upon landing should not cause a somatogravic illusion.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B)
explanation.kr: 이륙처럼 급가속하면 이석기관은 머리가 뒤로 기울어진 것과 비슷하게 자극된다. 시각 기준이 부족할 때 기수가 올라간 듯한 체성중력착각이 생길 수 있다.

question: To cope with spatial disorientation, pilots should rely on

choices.A: body sensations and outside visual references.
choices.B: adequate food, rest, and night adaptation.
choices.C: proficient use of the aircraft instruments.

explanation.en:
The most important way to cope with spatial disorientation is to become proficient in the use of flight instruments and rely on them.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Body sensations should be disregarded, not relied on, to cope with spatial disorientation. Outside visual references may be used to prevent spatial disorientation but only if they are reliable, fixed points on the earth's surface. Answer (B) is incorrect. Adequate food, rest, and night adaptions may help you be less susceptible to spatial disorientation but should not be relied on to cope with it.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 공간정위상실에 대응하는 가장 중요한 방법은 비행계기 사용에 숙달하고 계기를 신뢰하는 것이다.

question: A pilot who needs to overcome the effects of spatial disorientation should

choices.A: breathe rapidly.
choices.B: ignore the instruments and rely on body sensations.
choices.C: place a greater emphasis on the flight instruments.

explanation.en:
A pilot can overcome the effects of spatial disorientation by placing a greater emphasis on the flight instruments. Doing this will help the pilot ignore the kinesthetic sensations encountered during spatial disorientation.

Answer (A) is incorrect. Increasing the rate. of respiration will not help the pilot overcome spatial disorientation and can subsequently lead to hyperventilation. Answer (B) is incorrect. Relying on the sensations of the body will further increase the effects of spatial disorientation, not decrease the symptoms.

Source: (FAA-H-8083-25B Chap 17)
explanation.kr: 공간정위상실 중에는 신체 감각보다 비행계기를 우선한다. 계기에 집중하면 잘못된 운동감각을 무시하는 데 도움이 된다.

question: To scan properly for traffic, a pilot should

choices.A: slowly sweep the field of vision from one side to the other at intervals.
choices.B: concentrate on any peripheral movement detected.
choices.C: use a series of short, regularly spaced eye movements that bring successive areas of the sky into the central visual field.

explanation.en:
The most effective way to scan for other aircraft during the day is to use a series of short, regularly spaced eye movements that bring successive areas of the sky into your central vision. Each movement should not exceed 10°, and each area should be observed for at least 1 sec. to facilitate detection.

Answer (A) is incorrect. You must concentrate on different segments systematically. Answer (B) is incorrect. Peripheral movement will not be detected easily, especially under adverse conditions such as haze.

Source: (AIM Para 8-1-6)
explanation.kr: 주간 교통 탐색은 눈을 짧고 규칙적으로 이동시키며 각 구역을 중심시야에 넣는 방식이 효과적이다. 원문은 한 번에 10° 이하, 각 구역 최소 1초 관찰을 권한다.

question: Which technique should a pilot use to scan for traffic to the right and left during straight-and-level flight?

choices.A: Systematically focus on different segments of the sky for short intervals.
choices.B: Concentrate on relative movement detected in the peripheral vision area.
choices.C: Continuous sweeping of the windshield from right to left.

explanation.en:
Due to the fact that eyes can focus only on a narrow viewing area, effective scanning is accomplished with a series of short, regularly spaced eye movements that bring successive areas of the sky into the central vision field.

Answer (B) is incorrect. It concerns scanning for traffic at night. Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot must continually scan successive, small portions of the sky. The eyes can focus only on a narrow viewing area and require at least 1 sec. to detect a faraway object.
